    /// Dispatch as the identity that owns the lungs mount. Registration and the
    /// call share one connection, so the bridge admits the call as that identity
    /// and runs it through MutationEngine under the identity's own grants.
    pub async fn call_as_identity(
        bus_address: &str,
        plugin_id: &str,
        method_name: &str,
        method: &MethodDecl,
        arguments: Value,
        credential: Vec<u8>,
    ) -> Result<CallReceipt, LungsError> {
        validate_arguments(method, &arguments)?;
        let operation_id = uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
        let connection = connect_bus(bus_address).await?;
        let bootstrap = tokio::time::timeout(
            LUNGS_NEGOTIATION_TIMEOUT,
            Proxy::new(
                &connection,
                PLUGIN_BUS_NAME,
                IDENTITY_OBJECT_PATH,
                IDENTITY_INTERFACE,
            ),
        )
        .await
        .map_err(|_| LungsError::Transport("identity bootstrap proxy timed out".into()))?
        .map_err(|error| LungsError::Transport(format!("identity bootstrap proxy: {error}")))?;
        let registered: bool = tokio::time::timeout(
            LUNGS_NEGOTIATION_TIMEOUT,
            bootstrap.call("RegisterCurrentSender", &(credential,)),
        )
        .await
        .map_err(|_| LungsError::Transport("identity registration timed out".into()))?
        .map_err(|error| match refusal(&error) {
            true => LungsError::Registration(error.to_string()),
            false => LungsError::Transport(format!("register: {error}")),
        })?;
        if !registered {
            return Err(LungsError::Registration(
                "bridge declined the credential".into(),
            ));
        }
        let result = plugin_call(
            &connection,
            plugin_id,
            method_name,
            &arguments,
            &operation_id,
        )
        .await?;
        receipt(plugin_id, method_name, method, result, &operation_id)
    }
    
    /// Dispatch over the bridge's shared lungs socket. The connection first binds
    /// to this identity's session, so no credential crosses it. An empty session
    /// calls the no-argument container bootstrap; the bridge derives identity
    /// from its kernel peer and native Incus binding. A named session uses the
    /// host-root-only bootstrap. Both run through the identity's own grants.
    pub async fn call_over_socket(
        socket: &Path,
        session: &str,
        plugin_id: &str,
        method_name: &str,
        method: &MethodDecl,
        arguments: Value,
    ) -> Result<CallReceipt, LungsError> {
        validate_arguments(method, &arguments)?;
        let operation_id = uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
        let stream = tokio::time::timeout(
            LUNGS_NEGOTIATION_TIMEOUT,
            tokio::net::UnixStream::connect(socket),
        )
        .await
        .map_err(|_| LungsError::Transport("lungs socket connection timed out".into()))?
        .map_err(|error| LungsError::Transport(format!("connect to {}: {error}", socket.display())))?;
        let connection = tokio::time::timeout(
            LUNGS_NEGOTIATION_TIMEOUT,
            zbus::connection::Builder::unix_stream(stream)
                .p2p()
                .auth_mechanism(zbus::connection::AuthMechanism::Anonymous)
                .build(),
        )
        .await
        .map_err(|_| LungsError::Transport("lungs socket negotiation timed out".into()))?
        .map_err(|error| LungsError::Transport(format!("lungs socket: {error}")))?;
        let lungs = tokio::time::timeout(
            LUNGS_NEGOTIATION_TIMEOUT,
            Proxy::new(
                &connection,
                PLUGIN_BUS_NAME,
                LUNGS_OBJECT_PATH,
                LUNGS_INTERFACE,
            ),
        )
        .await
        .map_err(|_| LungsError::Transport("lungs bind proxy timed out".into()))?
        .map_err(|error| LungsError::Transport(format!("lungs bind proxy: {error}")))?;
        let binding = tokio::time::timeout(LUNGS_NEGOTIATION_TIMEOUT, async {
            if session.is_empty() {
                lungs.call("BindCurrentContainer", &()).await
            } else {
                lungs.call("Bind", &(session,)).await
            }
        })
        .await
        .map_err(|_| LungsError::Transport("lungs identity bind timed out".into()))?;
        let bound: bool = binding.map_err(|error| match refusal(&error) {
            true => LungsError::Registration(error.to_string()),
            false => LungsError::Transport(format!("bind: {error}")),
        })?;
        if !bound {
            return Err(LungsError::Registration(
                "bridge declined to bind this session".into(),
            ));
        }
        let result = plugin_call(
            &connection,
            plugin_id,
            method_name,
            &arguments,
            &operation_id,
        )
        .await?;
        receipt(plugin_id, method_name, method, result, &operation_id)
    }
    
    async fn connect_bus(bus_address: &str) -> Result<zbus::Connection, LungsError> {
        let builder = zbus::connection::Builder::address(bus_address)
            .map_err(|error| LungsError::Transport(format!("bus address {bus_address}: {error}")))?;
        tokio::time::timeout(LUNGS_NEGOTIATION_TIMEOUT, builder.build())
            .await
            .map_err(|_| LungsError::Transport("D-Bus connection timed out".into()))?
            .map_err(|error| LungsError::Transport(format!("connect to {bus_address}: {error}")))
    }
    
    async fn plugin_call(
        connection: &zbus::Connection,
        plugin_id: &str,
        method_name: &str,
        arguments: &Value,
        operation_id: &str,
    ) -> Result<Value, LungsError> {
        let proxy = tokio::time::timeout(
            LUNGS_NEGOTIATION_TIMEOUT,
            Proxy::new(
                connection,
                PLUGIN_BUS_NAME,
                format!("/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/{plugin_id}"),

## Assistant

You’re right. **The browser doesn’t need direct filesystem access.** 3tchedFS is a runtime projection of the sealed blob’s plugin schema, and the browser can call that same plugin method through the bridge.

I checked the dispatch:

- 3tchedFS projects `chat_router.Chat` and calls its D-Bus `CallWithOperationId`.
- The browser calls the same sealed `chat_router.Chat` method through `PluginService/CallMethod`.
- Both reach the bridge’s `chat_router` dispatch.

My earlier statement that a separate component had to open Wheelhouse’s mount was wrong. The call is already entering the blob-derived plugin surface; the failure occurs **after that**, when the bridge calls threetched and requires the missing SID1 acknowledgement.

The temporary bypass addresses that downstream failure, but its release rolled back during bridge readiness. It is not active.

    //! Thin tonic server: the three core services plus gRPC reflection.

    /// Serve `StateSync`, `PluginService` and `EventChainService` (plus
    /// reflection) on `addr`. Runs until the server errors.
    pub async fn serve(addr: SocketAddr, core: BridgeCore) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        serve_with_listener(TcpListener::bind(addr).await?, core).await
    }
    
    /// Serve on an already bound listener, retaining ownership of its address.
    pub async fn serve_with_listener(listener: TcpListener, core: BridgeCore) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let service = BridgeService::new(core);
        let reflection = tonic_reflection::server::Builder::configure()
            .register_encoded_file_descriptor_set(FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET)
            .build_v1()?;
        tonic::transport::Server::builder()
            .add_service(StateSyncServer::new(service.clone()))
            .add_service(PluginServiceServer::new(service.clone()))
            .add_service(EventChainServiceServer::new(service))
            .add_service(reflection)
            .serve_with_incoming(TcpListenerStream::new(listener))
            .await?;
        Ok(())
    }

    //!
    //! Every accepted mutation appends exactly one journal event and publishes
    //! exactly one [`StateChange`](crate::proto::StateChange) frame. Rejected
    //! mutations journal nothing. [`Journal::verify`] recomputes the chain, so

    use crate::catalog::Catalog;
    use crate::proto::{ChainEvent, ChangeType, Decision, ErrorCode, StateChange, StateFrameKind};
    use crate::router::{Handler, Router, RouterError};
    use prost_types::{Struct as ProtoStruct, Timestamp, Value as ProtoValue};
    use std::collections::HashMap;
    use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, RwLock};
    use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
    use tokio::sync::broadcast;
    
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Shared helpers
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    /// Current wall-clock time as a protobuf Timestamp.
    pub fn now_timestamp() -> Timestamp {
        let elapsed = SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
            .unwrap_or_default();
        Timestamp {
            seconds: elapsed.as_secs() as i64,
            nanos: elapsed.subsec_nanos() as i32,
        }
    }
    
    /// Canonical JSON bytes for hashing (`serde_json::Map` is a BTreeMap, so key
    /// order is stable).
    fn canonical_json(value: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<u8> {
        serde_json::to_vec(value).unwrap_or_default()
    }
    
    /// protobuf `Value` -> JSON. Non-finite doubles become null (JSON has no NaN).
    pub fn proto_value_to_json(value: &ProtoValue) -> serde_json::Value {
        use prost_types::value::Kind;
        match &value.kind {
            None | Some(Kind::NullValue(_)) => serde_json::Value::Null,
            Some(Kind::NumberValue(n)) => serde_json::Number::from_f64(*n)
                .map(serde_json::Value::Number)
                .unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null),
            Some(Kind::StringValue(s)) => serde_json::Value::String(s.clone()),
            Some(Kind::BoolValue(b)) => serde_json::Value::Bool(*b),
            Some(Kind::StructValue(s)) => serde_json::Value::Object(
                s.fields
                    .iter()
                    .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), proto_value_to_json(v)))
                    .collect(),
            ),
            Some(Kind::ListValue(l)) => {
                serde_json::Value::Array(l.values.iter().map(proto_value_to_json).collect())
            }
        }
    }
    
    /// JSON -> protobuf `Value`.
    pub fn json_to_proto_value(value: &serde_json::Value) -> ProtoValue {
        use prost_types::value::Kind;
        let kind = match value {
            serde_json::Value::Null => Kind::NullValue(0),
            serde_json::Value::Bool(b) => Kind::BoolValue(*b),
            serde_json::Value::Number(n) => Kind::NumberValue(n.as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0)),
            serde_json::Value::String(s) => Kind::StringValue(s.clone()),
            serde_json::Value::Array(items) => Kind::ListValue(prost_types::ListValue {
                values: items.iter().map(json_to_proto_value).collect(),
            }),
            serde_json::Value::Object(map) => Kind::StructValue(json_map_to_proto_struct(map)),
        };
        ProtoValue { kind: Some(kind) }
    }
    
    /// JSON object -> protobuf `Struct`.
    pub fn json_map_to_proto_struct(
        map: &serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
    ) -> ProtoStruct {
        ProtoStruct {
            fields: map
                .iter()
                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), json_to_proto_value(v)))
                .collect(),
        }
    }
    
    fn deep_merge(
        base: &mut serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
        patch: &serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
    ) {
        for (key, value) in patch {
            match (base.get_mut(key), value) {
                (Some(serde_json::Value::Object(b)), serde_json::Value::Object(p)) => {
                    deep_merge(b, p);
                }
                _ => {
                    base.insert(key.clone(), value.clone());
                }
            }
        }
    }

    //! Method router: `(plugin_id, method)` -> synchronous handler.
    //!
    //! Handlers are pure value-in/value-out functions over JSON values. Async or
    //! D-Bus-backed behavior plugs in behind [`BridgeCore`](crate::core::BridgeCore)
    //! call sites, not inside the router.
    
    use std::collections::HashMap;
    use std::sync::{Arc, RwLock};
    
    /// A synchronous value-in/value-out method handler.
    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub struct Handler(
        Arc<dyn Fn(&[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<serde_json::Value, RouterError> + Send + Sync>,
    );
    
    impl Handler {
        /// Wrap a plain closure as a handler.
        pub fn new<F>(f: F) -> Self
        where
            F: Fn(&[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<serde_json::Value, RouterError>
                + Send
                + Sync
                + 'static,
        {
            Self(Arc::new(f))
        }
    
        /// Run the handler.
        pub fn call(&self, args: &[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<serde_json::Value, RouterError> {
            (self.0)(args)
        }
    }
    
    impl<F> From<F> for Handler
    where
        F: Fn(&[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<serde_json::Value, RouterError> + Send + Sync + 'static,
    {
        fn from(f: F) -> Self {
            Self::new(f)
        }
    }
    
    impl std::fmt::Debug for Handler {
        fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
            f.write_str("Handler(..)")
        }
    }
    
    /// Router failure: unknown route, or a handler that returned an error.
    #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
    pub enum RouterError {
        /// No route table entry for this plugin at all.
        #[error("unknown plugin: {0}")]
        UnknownPlugin(String),
        /// Plugin is routed, but this method is not.
        #[error("unknown method '{method}' for plugin '{plugin_id}'")]
        UnknownMethod { plugin_id: String, method: String },
        /// The handler ran and failed.
        #[error("handler for '{plugin_id}.{method}' failed: {message}")]
        HandlerFailed {
            plugin_id: String,
            method: String,
            message: String,
        },
    }
    
    /// Synchronous `(plugin_id, method)` dispatch table. Cheap to clone.
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
    pub struct Router {
        routes: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, HashMap<String, Handler>>>>,
    }
    
    impl Router {
        /// An empty router.
        pub fn new() -> Self {
            Self::default()
        }
    
        /// Register (or replace) the handler for one route.
        pub fn register(
            &self,
            plugin_id: impl Into<String>,
            method: impl Into<String>,
            handler: Handler,
        ) {
            self.routes
                .write()
                .expect("router lock poisoned")
                .entry(plugin_id.into())
                .or_default()
                .insert(method.into(), handler);
        }
    
        /// Is a handler registered for this route?
        pub fn has(&self, plugin_id: &str, method: &str) -> bool {
            self.routes
                .read()
                .expect("router lock poisoned")
                .get(plugin_id)
                .is_some_and(|methods| methods.contains_key(method))
        }
    
        /// Dispatch one call. The table lock is released before the handler runs.
        pub fn call(
            &self,
            plugin_id: &str,
            method: &str,
            args: &[serde_json::Value],
        ) -> Result<serde_json::Value, RouterError> {
            let handler = {
                let routes = self.routes.read().expect("router lock poisoned");
                let methods = routes
                    .get(plugin_id)
                    .ok_or_else(|| RouterError::UnknownPlugin(plugin_id.to_string()))?;
                methods
                    .get(method)
                    .cloned()
                    .ok_or_else(|| RouterError::UnknownMethod {
                        plugin_id: plugin_id.to_string(),
                        method: method.to_string(),
                    })?
            };
            handler.call(args).map_err(|err| match err {
                // A handler that returns routing errors is confused; normalize.
                RouterError::HandlerFailed { .. } => err,
                other => RouterError::HandlerFailed {
                    plugin_id: plugin_id.to_string(),
                    method: method.to_string(),
                    message: other.to_string(),
                },
            })
        }
    }

    # A2A Protocol
    
    ## Overview
    
    The Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol lets agents built on different frameworks discover each other through an Agent Card, exchange messages, and run long-lived tasks without exposing their internals. The current spec is **1.0** (a2a-protocol.org/v1.0.0/specification) with three bindings: JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP, HTTP+JSON/REST and gRPC; streaming uses SSE and async work can use webhook push notifications. This skill was checked against `a2a-sdk` 1.2.1 (Python) and `@a2a-js/sdk` 1.3.0.
    
    Most tutorials online still show the 0.2/0.3 API (`A2AStarletteApplication`, `TextPart`, `/.well-known/agent.json`, `A2AClient`). Those no longer exist in 1.x. If a project pins `a2a-sdk<1`, follow the SDK's v0.3 to v1.0 migration guide (docs/migrations/v1_0 in the a2a-python repo) rather than mixing styles.
    
    ## Instructions
    
    ### 1. Core concepts (v1.0)
    
    - **Agent Card**: JSON served at `/.well-known/agent-card.json`. Lists name, version, `supportedInterfaces` (one entry per transport: `protocolBinding` `JSONRPC`, `HTTP+JSON` or `GRPC`, plus `url`), capabilities, skills and security schemes. There is no top-level `url` any more.
    - **Task**: stateful unit of work. States: `TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED`, `WORKING`, `INPUT_REQUIRED`, `AUTH_REQUIRED`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED`, `REJECTED`.
    - **Message**: one turn with `role` (`ROLE_USER` / `ROLE_AGENT`) and `parts`. A `Part` is a single unified type with `text`, `raw` (bytes), `url` or `data`; the old `TextPart`/`FilePart`/`DataPart` wrappers are gone.
    - **Artifact**: output of a task (documents, files, structured data).
    - Enum names in the SDKs are SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (`TaskState.TASK_STATE_WORKING`, `Role.ROLE_USER`).
    
    ### 2. Install
    
    ```bash
    pip install "a2a-sdk[http-server]"   # core + Starlette/SSE server pieces
    pip install "a2a-sdk[grpc]"          # gRPC; also: [fastapi] [postgresql] [mysql] [sqlite] [telemetry] [all]
    npm install @a2a-js/sdk express      # Node; express is a peer dependency of the server helpers
    ```
    
    ### 3. Server in Python
    
    A server must follow one of two streaming patterns, or the SDK raises `InvalidAgentResponseError`: enqueue exactly one `Message`, or enqueue a `Task` first and then status/artifact updates until a terminal state. Never mix them.
    
    ```python
    import uvicorn
    from starlette.applications import Starlette
    from a2a.helpers import (new_task_from_user_message, new_text_artifact_update_event,
                             new_text_status_update_event)
    from a2a.server.agent_execution import AgentExecutor, RequestContext
    from a2a.server.events import EventQueue
    from a2a.server.request_handlers import DefaultRequestHandler
    from a2a.server.routes import create_agent_card_routes, create_jsonrpc_routes
    from a2a.server.tasks import InMemoryTaskStore
    from a2a.types import AgentCapabilities, AgentCard, AgentInterface, AgentSkill, TaskState
    
    class BillingAgent(AgentExecutor):
        async def execute(self, context: RequestContext, event_queue: EventQueue):
            task = context.current_task or new_task_from_user_message(context.message)
            await event_queue.enqueue_event(task)                      # Task first
            await event_queue.enqueue_event(new_text_status_update_event(
                task_id=task.id, context_id=task.context_id,
                state=TaskState.TASK_STATE_WORKING, text="Looking up the invoice..."))
            answer = f"Invoice INV-2041 is paid. You asked: {context.get_user_input()}"
            await event_queue.enqueue_event(new_text_artifact_update_event(
                task_id=task.id, context_id=task.context_id, name="answer", text=answer))
            await event_queue.enqueue_event(new_text_status_update_event(
                task_id=task.id, context_id=task.context_id,
                state=TaskState.TASK_STATE_COMPLETED, text="Done"))
    
        async def cancel(self, context: RequestContext, event_queue: EventQueue):
            await event_queue.enqueue_event(new_text_status_update_event(
                task_id=context.task_id, context_id=context.context_id,
                state=TaskState.TASK_STATE_CANCELED, text="Canceled"))
    
    card = AgentCard(
        name="Billing Agent", description="Answers questions about invoices.", version="1.0.0",
        supported_interfaces=[AgentInterface(protocol_binding="JSONRPC", url="http://127.0.0.1:9000/")],
        capabilities=AgentCapabilities(streaming=True),
        default_input_modes=["text/plain"], default_output_modes=["text/plain"],
        skills=[AgentSkill(id="invoice-status", name="Invoice status",
                           description="Look up whether an invoice is paid", tags=["billing"],
                           examples=["Is invoice INV-2041 paid?"])],
    )
    handler = DefaultRequestHandler(agent_executor=BillingAgent(), task_store=InMemoryTaskStore(),
                                    agent_card=card)          # agent_card is required in 1.x
    app = Starlette(routes=[*create_agent_card_routes(card),
                            *create_jsonrpc_routes(handler, rpc_url="/")])
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=9000)
    ```
    
    `create_rest_routes(handler)` adds the HTTP+JSON binding (declare it in `supported_interfaces` too). To serve old 0.3 clients as well, add a 0.3 `AgentInterface` with `protocol_version="0.3"` and pass `enable_v0_3_compat=True` to the route factories.
    //! Thin tonic translation of the three core proto services onto [`BridgeCore`].
    //!
    //! `EventChainService` proof/snapshot RPCs are honestly `UNIMPLEMENTED`;
    //! everything else is real. `OvsdbMirror`, `RuntimeMirror` and
    //! `DbusPassthrough` are generated from the same file but not served: the
    //! fresh bridge owns state, plugins and audit only.
    
    use crate::core::{
        json_map_to_proto_struct, json_to_proto_value, proto_value_to_json, BridgeCore, CoreMutation,
        CoreOperation, CoreRejection, JournalEvent, MutationOutcome,
    };
    use crate::proto::event_chain_service_server::EventChainService;
    use crate::proto::plugin_service_server::PluginService;
    use crate::proto::state_sync_server::StateSync;
    use crate::proto::{
        BatchMutateRequest, BatchMutateResponse, CallMethodRequest, CallMethodResponse, ChainEvent,
        ChangeType, CreateSnapshotRequest, CreateSnapshotResponse, Decision, ErrorCode,
        GetEventsRequest, GetEventsResponse, GetProofRequest, GetProofResponse, GetPropertyRequest,
        GetPropertyResponse, GetSchemaRequest, GetSchemaResponse, GetSnapshotRequest,
        GetSnapshotResponse, GetStateRequest, GetStateResponse, ListPluginsResponse, MutateRequest,
        MutateResponse, MutationError, OperationType, PluginInfo, ProveTagImmutabilityRequest,
        ProveTagImmutabilityResponse, SearchSemanticTraceRequest, SearchSemanticTraceResponse,
        SemanticTraceMatch, SetPropertyRequest, SetPropertyResponse, Signal, StateChange,
        SubscribeEventsRequest, SubscribeRequest, SubscribeSignalsRequest, VerifyChainRequest,
        VerifyChainResponse,
    };
    use tokio::sync::{broadcast, mpsc};
    use tokio_stream::wrappers::ReceiverStream;
    use tonic::{Request, Response, Status};
    
    /// The three core services, backed by one [`BridgeCore`].
    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub struct BridgeService {
        core: BridgeCore,
    }
    
    impl BridgeService {
        /// Serve `core` over tonic.
        pub fn new(core: BridgeCore) -> Self {
            Self { core }
        }
    }
    
    fn mutation_error(code: ErrorCode, message: String) -> MutationError {
        MutationError {
            code: code as i32,
            message,
            deny_reason: None,
        }
    }
    
    /// Translate one wire mutation. Infallible: anything malformed becomes a
    /// [`CoreOperation`] the core rejects at admission, so batch alignment
    /// never depends on translation order.
    fn core_mutation(req: &MutateRequest, actor_default: &str) -> CoreMutation {
        let operation = if req.operation == OperationType::SetProperty as i32 {
            CoreOperation::SetProperty
        } else if req.operation == OperationType::CallMethod as i32 {
            CoreOperation::CallMethod
        } else if req.operation == OperationType::ApplyPatch as i32 {
            CoreOperation::ApplyPatch
        } else {
            CoreOperation::Unknown
        };
        CoreMutation {
            plugin_id: req.plugin_id.clone(),
            object_path: req.object_path.clone(),
            operation,
            member_name: req.member_name.clone(),
            value: req
                .value
                .as_ref()
                .map(proto_value_to_json)
                .unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null),
            actor_id: if req.actor_id.is_empty() {
                actor_default.to_string()
            } else {
                req.actor_id.clone()
            },
            capability_id: req.capability_id.clone(),
            idempotency_key: req.idempotency_key.clone(),
        }
    }
    
    fn mutate_response(result: Result<MutationOutcome, CoreRejection>) -> MutateResponse {
        match result {
            Ok(outcome) => MutateResponse {
                success: true,
                event_id: outcome.event.event_id,
                event_hash: outcome.event.event_hash,
                result: outcome.result.as_ref().map(json_to_proto_value),
                error: None,
                effective_hash: outcome.event.result_effective_hash,
            },
            Err(rejection) => MutateResponse {
                success: false,
                event_id: 0,
                event_hash: String::new(),
                result: None,
                error: Some(mutation_error(rejection.code, rejection.message)),
                effective_hash: String::new(),
            },
        }
    }
    
    /// Tiny glob over bytes: `*` matches any run, `?` matches one byte.
    fn glob_match(pattern: &str, text: &str) -> bool {
        fn walk(pattern: &[u8], text: &[u8]) -> bool {
            if pattern.is_empty() {
                return text.is_empty();
            }
            match pattern[0] {
                b'*' => (0..=text.len()).any(|split| walk(&pattern[1..], &text[split..])),
                b'?' => !text.is_empty() && walk(&pattern[1..], &text[1..]),
                byte => !text.is_empty() && text[0] == byte && walk(&pattern[1..], &text[1..]),
            }
        }
        walk(pattern.as_bytes(), text.as_bytes())
    }
    
    fn state_matches(req: &SubscribeRequest, frame: &StateChange) -> bool {
        (req.plugin_ids.is_empty() || req.plugin_ids.contains(&frame.plugin_id))
            && (req.path_patterns.is_empty()
                || req
                    .path_patterns
                    .iter()
                    .any(|pattern| glob_match(pattern, &frame.object_path)))
            && (req.tags.is_empty()
                || frame
                    .tags_touched
                    .iter()
                    .any(|tag| req.tags.contains(tag)))
    }
    
    fn chain_matches(req: &SubscribeEventsRequest, event: &ChainEvent) -> bool {
        (req.plugin_id.is_empty() || event.plugin_id == req.plugin_id)
            && (req.tags.is_empty()
                || event
                    .tags_touched
                    .iter()
                    .any(|tag| req.tags.contains(tag)))
    }
    
    /// Event summary carried in each trace-match payload.
    fn event_payload(event: &JournalEvent) -> serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> {
        serde_json::Map::from_iter([
            ("event_id".to_string(), serde_json::json!(event.event_id)),
            (
                "event_hash".to_string(),
                serde_json::json!(event.event_hash),
            ),
            ("plugin_id".to_string(), serde_json::json!(event.plugin_id)),
            (
                "operation_type".to_string(),
                serde_json::json!(event.operation_type),
            ),
            ("target".to_string(), serde_json::json!(event.target)),
            ("actor_id".to_string(), serde_json::json!(event.actor_id)),
        ])
    }
    
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // StateSync
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    #[async_trait::async_trait]
    impl StateSync for BridgeService {
        type SubscribeStream = ReceiverStream<Result<StateChange, Status>>;
    
        async fn subscribe(
            &self,
            request: Request<SubscribeRequest>,
        ) -> Result<Response<Self::SubscribeStream>, Status> {
            let req = request.into_inner();
            // Register before returning the RPC, and snapshot under the same
            // commit boundary. No updates can fall between hydration and live.
            let (initial, schemas, mut sub) = self.core.state_subscription(
                req.include_initial_state,
                req.include_schema,
            );
            let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel(128);
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                for frame in initial {
                    if state_matches(&req, &frame) && tx.send(Ok(frame)).await.is_err() {
                        return;
                    }
                }
                for frame in schemas {
                    // Contracts carry no path or tags; the plugin filter still applies.
                    if !req.plugin_ids.is_empty() && !req.plugin_ids.contains(&frame.plugin_id) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    if tx.send(Ok(frame)).await.is_err() {
                        return;
                    }
                }
                loop {
                    let received = tokio::select! {
                        _ = tx.closed() => return,
                        received = sub.recv() => received,
                    };
                    match received {
                        Ok(frame) => {
                            if state_matches(&req, &frame) && tx.send(Ok(frame)).await.is_err() {
                                return;
                            }
                        }
                        Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(skipped)) => {
                            let _ = tx.send(Err(Status::data_loss(format!(
                                "state stream missed {skipped} updates; resubscribe with include_initial_state",
                            )))).await;
                            return;
                        }
                        Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => return,
                    }
                }
            });
            Ok(Response::new(ReceiverStream::new(rx)))
        }

    /// Require the sealed method's exact capability and the principal's exact grant.
    /// The grant document must come from the protected grant projection, never a caller.
    pub(crate) fn require_method_grant(
        identity: &VerifiedSid1,
        catalog_dir: &Path,
        plugin_id: &str,
        canonical_method: &str,
        requested_capability: Option<&str>,
        grants: &serde_json::Value,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<(MethodDecl, String)> {
        let pinned = crate::catalog::Catalog::sealed_plugin(catalog_dir, plugin_id)?;
        let schema: PluginSchema = serde_json::from_value(
            pinned
                .schema
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("sealed plugin schema is unavailable"))?,
        )?;
        let declaration = schema
            .methods
            .get(canonical_method)
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("sealed method is unavailable"))?;
        let required = declaration
            .required_capability
            .as_deref()
            .map(str::trim)
            .filter(|capability| !capability.is_empty())
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("sealed method capability is unavailable"))?;
        let claims = identity.claims();
        anyhow::ensure!(
            !claims.principal_id.is_empty() && !claims.session_id.is_empty(),
            "verified identity is incomplete"
        );
        anyhow::ensure!(
            claims.expires_at == 0 || claims.expires_at > chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
            "verified identity has expired"
        );
        anyhow::ensure!(
            requested_capability == Some(required),
            "requested capability does not match the sealed method"
        );
        anyhow::ensure!(
            crate::grant_document::capabilities_for_principal(grants, &claims.principal_id)
                .contains(required),
            "principal lacks the required capability"
        );
        Ok((declaration.clone(), pinned.schema_hash))
    }

        async fn call_method(
            &self,
            request: Request<CallMethodRequest>,
        ) -> Result<Response<CallMethodResponse>, Status> {
            let req = request.into_inner();
            // Routes key on (plugin, method); interface_name is informational.
            let args: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
                req.arguments.iter().map(proto_value_to_json).collect();
            let op = CoreMutation {
                plugin_id: req.plugin_id.clone(),
                object_path: req.object_path.clone(),
                operation: CoreOperation::CallMethod,
                member_name: req.method_name.clone(),
                value: serde_json::Value::Array(args),
                actor_id: req.actor_id.clone(),
                capability_id: req.capability_id.clone(),
                idempotency_key: String::new(),
            };
            match self.core.mutate(op) {
                Ok(outcome) => Ok(Response::new(CallMethodResponse {
                    success: true,
                    result: outcome.result.as_ref().map(json_to_proto_value),
                    event_id: outcome.event.event_id,
                    event_hash: outcome.event.event_hash,
                    error: None,
                })),
                Err(rejection) => Ok(Response::new(CallMethodResponse {
                    success: false,
                    result: None,
                    event_id: 0,
                    event_hash: String::new(),
                    error: Some(mutation_error(rejection.code, rejection.message)),

    fn pinned_identity(dir: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<crate::catalog::PluginEntry> {
        let pinned = Catalog::sealed_plugin(dir, "identity_sled")?;
        let schema: op_state_store::PluginSchema = serde_json::from_value(
            pinned
                .schema
                .clone()
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("sealed identity schema absent"))?,
        )?;
        let compiled: CompiledIdentityContract = serde_json::from_str(include_str!(concat!(
            env!("OUT_DIR"),
            "/identity_state_contract.json"
        )))?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            schema.version == compiled.version && schema.fields == compiled.fields,
            "compiled and sealed identity state contracts differ"
        );
        Ok(pinned)
    }
    
    fn committed_session(
        catalog_dir: &Path,
        state_dir: &str,
        session_id: &str,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<Option<ContainerIdentitySled>> {
        let before = pinned_identity(catalog_dir)?;
        let bytes =
            op_core::projection_shm::read_credential_projection_bytes_in(state_dir, "identity_sled")?
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("committed identity credential projection is absent"))?;
        let after = pinned_identity(catalog_dir)?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            before.schema_hash == after.schema_hash
                && before.sealed_schema_json == after.sealed_schema_json,
            "identity plugin seal changed during credential state access"
        );
        let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            value.get("sleds").is_some_and(serde_json::Value::is_array),
            "identity sleds missing"
        );
        anyhow::ensure!(
            value.get("events").is_some_and(serde_json::Value::is_array),
            "identity events missing"
        );
        let state: IdentitySledState = serde_json::from_value(value)?;
        let mut ids = HashSet::new();
        for sled in &state.sleds {
            anyhow::ensure!(
                ids.insert(sled.session_id.as_str()),
                "duplicate identity in SHM"
            );
            crate::identity_binding::validate_sled(sled)?;
        }
        let mut events = HashSet::new();
        for event in &state.events {
            anyhow::ensure!(
                events.insert((event.session_id.as_str(), event.seq)),
                "duplicate identity event in SHM"
            );
        }
        Ok(state
            .sleds
            .into_iter()
            .find(|sled| sled.session_id == session_id))
    }
    
    pub(crate) fn verify_in(
        catalog_dir: &Path,
        state_dir: &str,
        wire: &[u8],
        transport: &str,
        now: i64,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<BoundSid1> {
        let claims =
            crate::sid1_checks::parse_for_transport(wire, transport).map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?;
        let sled = committed_session(catalog_dir, state_dir, &claims.session_id)?
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("sealed identity session was not found"))?;
        let claims = crate::sid1_checks::match_bound_session(wire, &sled, transport, now)
            .map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?;
        Ok(BoundSid1(claims))
    }

    pub(crate) fn bound_session_for_key_in(

        );

    use std::convert::Infallible;

    use std::sync::Arc;

    /// Keep the selected PEM pair available to the upgrade-capable TCP server.
    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub struct PemIdentity {
        cert: Vec<u8>,
        key: Vec<u8>,
    }
    
    impl std::fmt::Debug for PemIdentity {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str("PemIdentity([redacted])")
        }
    }
    
    impl PemIdentity {
        pub fn from_pem(cert: impl AsRef<[u8]>, key: impl AsRef<[u8]>) -> Self {
            Self {
                cert: cert.as_ref().to_vec(),
                key: key.as_ref().to_vec(),
            }
        }
    
        pub fn server_config(&self) -> anyhow::Result<Arc<rustls::ServerConfig>> {
            let certs = rustls_pemfile::certs(&mut BufReader::new(self.cert.as_slice()))
                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
            anyhow::ensure!(!certs.is_empty(), "TCP TLS certificate chain is empty");
            let key = rustls_pemfile::private_key(&mut BufReader::new(self.key.as_slice()))?
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("TCP TLS private key is missing"))?;
            let mut config = rustls::ServerConfig::builder_with_provider(Arc::new(
                rustls::crypto::aws_lc_rs::default_provider(),
            ))
            .with_safe_default_protocol_versions()?
            .with_no_client_auth()
            .with_single_cert(certs, key)?;
            config.alpn_protocols = vec![b"h2".to_vec(), b"http/1.1".to_vec()];
            Ok(Arc::new(config))
        }
    }
    
    /// Serve `app` over TLS on `listener`, allowing HTTP/1 upgrades
    /// (websockets). Runs until the listener errors.
    pub async fn serve_upgradeable_tcp(
        listener: tokio::net::TcpListener,
        tls: Arc<rustls::ServerConfig>,
        app: Router,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        const MAX_CONNECTIONS: usize = 512;
        let permits = Arc::new(tokio::sync::Semaphore::new(MAX_CONNECTIONS));
        let acceptor = TlsAcceptor::from(tls);
        loop {
            let permit = permits.clone().acquire_owned().await?;
            let (stream, peer) = match listener.accept().await {
                Ok(accepted) => accepted,
                Err(error) => {
                    tracing::warn!(%error, "TCP door accept failed");
                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)).await;
                    continue;
                }
            };
            let acceptor = acceptor.clone();
            let app = app.clone();
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                let permit = Arc::new(permit);
                let tls =
                    match tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), acceptor.accept(stream)).await {
                        Ok(Ok(tls)) => tls,
                        _ => return,
                    };
                let service = hyper::service::service_fn(move |request: hyper::Request<Incoming>| {
                    let mut app = app.clone();
                    let permit = permit.clone();
                    async move {
                        let mut request = request.map(Body::new);
                        request.extensions_mut().insert(ConnectInfo(peer));
                        request.extensions_mut().insert(permit);
                        let response = app.call(request).await?;
                        Ok::<_, Infallible>(response)
                    }
                });
                let mut builder = Builder::new(TokioExecutor::new());
                builder
                    .http1()
                    .timer(TokioTimer::new())
                    .header_read_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10));
                if let Err(error) = builder
                    .serve_connection_with_upgrades(TokioIo::new(tls), service)
                    .await
                {
                    tracing::debug!(%error, "TCP door connection closed");
                }
            });
        }
    }

        #[serde(default)]
        pub name: String,
        #[serde(default)]
        pub version: String,
        #[serde(default)]
        pub description: String,
        #[serde(default)]
        pub dbus_path: String,
        #[serde(default)]
        pub interfaces: Vec<String>,
        #[serde(default)]
        pub tags: Vec<String>,
        /// Hash of this plugin's current schema; stamped on its frames.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub schema_hash: String,
        /// JSON Schema for the plugin, when the catalog carries it.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub schema: Option<serde_json::Value>,
        /// Exact schema bytes from the sealed blob, retained for pin comparisons.
        #[serde(skip)]
        pub sealed_schema_json: Option<String>,
        #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "de_methods")]
        pub methods: Vec<PluginMethod>,
    }
    
    fn de_methods<'de, D>(d: D) -> Result<Vec<PluginMethod>, D::Error>
    where
        D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,
    {
        #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
        #[serde(untagged)]
        enum M {
            Named(PluginMethod),
            Plain(String),
        }
        Ok(Vec::<M>::deserialize(d)?
            .into_iter()
            .map(|m| match m {
                M::Named(p) => p,
                M::Plain(s) => PluginMethod::from(s),
            })
            .collect())
    }
    
    /// The whole plugin catalog.
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
    pub struct Catalog {
        plugins: Vec<PluginEntry>,
        by_id: BTreeMap<String, usize>,
        hash: String,
    }
    
    fn read_sealed_entry(dir: &Path, id: &str, schema_hash: &str) -> anyhow::Result<PluginEntry> {
        let schema = op_blob::catalog::read_plugin_state_store_schema(dir, id)
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid sealed plugin {id}"))?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            schema_hash.len() == 64 && schema_hash.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()),
            "invalid schema hash for {id}"
        );
        let bytes = std::fs::read(dir.join(format!("{id}.{}.blob", &schema_hash[..16])))?;
        let blob = op_blob::BlobRef::from_manifest_pinned(&bytes, schema_hash)
            .map_err(|error| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid sealed plugin {id}: {error}"))?;
        let pinned_schema = blob
            .state_store_schema()
            .map_err(|error| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid sealed plugin {id}: {error}"))?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            serde_json::to_value(&schema)? == serde_json::to_value(&pinned_schema)?,
            "sealed plugin {id} changed during read"
        );
        let raw_schema = serde_json::from_str(blob.schema_json())?;
        let mut methods: Vec<_> = schema
            .methods
            .keys()
            .cloned()
            .map(PluginMethod::from)
            .collect();
        methods.sort_by(|a, b| a.name.cmp(&b.name));
        Ok(PluginEntry {
            id: id.to_owned(),
            name: schema.name,
            version: schema.version,
            description: schema.description,
            dbus_path: format!("/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/{id}"),
            tags: schema.tags,
            schema_hash: schema_hash.to_owned(),
            schema: Some(raw_schema),
            sealed_schema_json: Some(blob.schema_json().to_owned()),
            methods,
            ..Default::default()
        })
    }
    
    impl Catalog {
        /// Read one consistent manifest-pinned snapshot of the sealed plugin catalog.
        /// The catalog identity comes from the sealer's manifest, never a consumer hash.
        pub fn from_sealed(dir: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<Self> {
            let manifest_path = dir.join(op_blob::catalog::MANIFEST_FILENAME);
            let manifest_bytes = std::fs::read(&manifest_path)?;
            let manifest: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&manifest_bytes)?;
            let catalog_hash = manifest["catalog_hash"]
                .as_str()
                .filter(|hash| hash.len() == 64 && hash.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()))
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid sealed catalog hash"))?
                .to_owned();
            let entries: BTreeMap<String, String> =
                serde_json::from_value(manifest["plugins"].clone())?;
            let mut plugins = Vec::with_capacity(entries.len());
            for (id, schema_hash) in entries {
                plugins.push(read_sealed_entry(dir, &id, &schema_hash)?);
            }
            anyhow::ensure!(
                std::fs::read(manifest_path)? == manifest_bytes,
                "sealed catalog changed during read"
            );
            let by_id = plugins
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .map(|(index, plugin)| (plugin.id.clone(), index))
                .collect();
            Ok(Self {
                plugins,
                by_id,
                hash: catalog_hash,
            })
        }
    
        /// Read a single manifest-pinned plugin without scanning other blobs.
        pub fn sealed_plugin(dir: &Path, id: &str) -> anyhow::Result<PluginEntry> {
            let path = dir.join(op_blob::catalog::MANIFEST_FILENAME);
            let before = std::fs::read(&path)?;
            let manifest: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&before)?;
            let hash = manifest["plugins"]
                .get(id)
                .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("sealed plugin {id} is absent"))?;
            let entry = read_sealed_entry(dir, id, hash)?;
            anyhow::ensure!(
                std::fs::read(path)? == before,
                "sealed catalog changed during read"
            );
            Ok(entry)
        }
    
        /// An empty catalog (hash of the empty pair set).
        pub fn empty() -> Self {
            Self::from_entries(Vec::new()).expect("empty catalog is valid")
        }
    
        /// Parse a catalog from any accepted JSON shape.
        pub fn from_json_str(text: &str) -> Result<Self, CatalogError> {
            let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(text)?;
            let entries = value
                .get("plugins")
                .or_else(|| value.get("entries"))
                .cloned()
                .unwrap_or(value);
            let plugins: Vec<PluginEntry> = serde_json::from_value(entries)?;
            Self::from_entries(plugins)
        }
    
        /// Build a catalog from entries, computing the catalog hash.
        pub fn from_entries(plugins: Vec<PluginEntry>) -> Result<Self, CatalogError> {
            let mut by_id = BTreeMap::new();
            for (i, p) in plugins.iter().enumerate() {
                if by_id.insert(p.id.clone(), i).is_some() {
                    return Err(CatalogError::Duplicate(p.id.clone()));
                }
            }
            let mut pairs: Vec<String> = plugins
                .iter()
                .map(|p| format!("{}={}", p.id, p.schema_hash))
                .collect();
            pairs.sort();
            let hash = blake3::hash(pairs.join("\n").as_bytes())
                .to_hex()
                .to_string();
            Ok(Self {
                plugins,
                by_id,
                hash,
            })
        }
    
        /// blake3 over the sorted `(plugin_id, schema_hash)` pairs.
        pub fn hash(&self) -> &str {
            &self.hash
        }
    
        pub fn plugins(&self) -> &[PluginEntry] {

    use std::os::fd::{AsRawFd, FromRawFd};
    use std::os::unix::fs::{MetadataExt, OpenOptionsExt};
    use std::path::{Component, Path, PathBuf};
    use std::sync::Arc;
    
    use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail, ensure};
    use serde_json::Value;
    
    use crate::dispatch;
    use crate::model::{MethodDecl, PluginSchema, TypedObjectBlob};
    use crate::namespace::{MountIdentity, encode_component};
    
    const MAX_DOCUMENT: u64 = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
    const MAX_RECEIPT: u64 = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
    
    type MountProbe = Arc<dyn Fn(&Path, &File) -> Result<String> + Send + Sync>;
    
    /// Preserve the original mounted denial without retrying or rewriting it.
    #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
    #[error("{0}")]
    pub struct MountedDiagnostic(pub Value);
    
    pub struct MountedNamespace {
        path: PathBuf,
        root: File,
        mount_id: String,
        metadata: Value,
        view: Value,
        probe: MountProbe,
    }
    
    impl MountedNamespace {
        pub fn open(path: &Path, expected_session: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self> {
            Self::open_with_probe(path, expected_session, Arc::new(probe_mount))
        }
    
        pub fn open_for_mode(path: &Path, expected: &MountIdentity) -> Result<Self> {
            ensure!(
                !matches!(expected, MountIdentity::Unbound),
                "unbound mount has no operation identity"
            );
            Self::open_with_mode_and_probe(path, None, Some(expected), Arc::new(probe_mount))
        }
    
        fn open_with_probe(
            path: &Path,
            expected_session: Option<&str>,
            probe: MountProbe,
        ) -> Result<Self> {
            Self::open_with_mode_and_probe(path, expected_session, None, probe)
        }
    
        fn open_with_mode_and_probe(
            path: &Path,
            expected_session: Option<&str>,
            expected_mode: Option<&MountIdentity>,
            probe: MountProbe,
        ) -> Result<Self> {
            let path = std::fs::canonicalize(path).context("resolve mounted namespace")?;
            let root = OpenOptions::new()
                .read(true)
                .custom_flags(libc::O_DIRECTORY | libc::O_NOFOLLOW | libc::O_CLOEXEC)
                .open(&path)
                .context("open mounted namespace")?;
            let mount_id = probe(&path, &root)?;
            let metadata = read_json(open_relative(&root, ".3tchedfs.json", false)?)?;
            ensure!(
                metadata["format"] == "3tchedfs/1",
                "unsupported mount declaration"
            );
            ensure!(
                metadata["workspace_id"].is_null(),
                "mount must be an identity view"
            );
            let instance = metadata["instance_uuid"]
                .as_str()
                .context("mount instance UUID absent")?;
            ensure!(
                uuid::Uuid::parse_str(instance)?.to_string() == instance,
                "mount instance UUID is noncanonical"
            );
            let mode: MountIdentity = serde_json::from_value(metadata["mount_identity"].clone())
                .context("mounted namespace has no typed identity mode")?;
            if let Some(expected) = expected_mode {
                ensure!(
                    &mode == expected,
                    "mounted identity mode differs from expected mode"
                );
            }
            match &mode {
                MountIdentity::HostSession { session } => {
                    ensure!(
                        !session.is_empty()
                            && metadata["session_id"].as_str() == Some(session.as_str()),
                        "mounted host session declaration is inconsistent"
                    );
                    if let Some(expected) = expected_session {
                        ensure!(
                            session == expected,
                            "mounted identity session differs from --expected-session"
                        );
                    }
                }
                MountIdentity::GuestKernel | MountIdentity::Credential => {
                    ensure!(
                        expected_mode.is_some() && metadata["session_id"].is_null(),
                        "mount must declare the expected operation identity mode"
                    );
                }
                MountIdentity::Unbound => bail!("unbound mount has no operation identity"),
            }
            let view = read_json(open_relative(&root, "view.json", false)?)?;
            for key in [
                "format",
                "view_id",
                "source_catalog_hash",
                "source_catalog_generation",
            ] {
                ensure!(
                    metadata.get(key).is_some() && metadata[key] == view[key],
                    "mount/view {key} mismatch"
                );
            }
            ensure!(
                view["objects"].is_object(),
                "mounted view has no object catalog"
            );
            ensure!(
                metadata["object_count"].as_u64()
                    == view["objects"]
                        .as_object()
                        .map(|objects| objects.len() as u64),
                "mounted catalog count mismatch"
            );
            let namespace = Self {
                path,
                root,
                mount_id,
                metadata,
                view,
                probe,
            };
            namespace.verify()?;
            Ok(namespace)
        }
    
        /// Pin the mount instance as well as its declared identity/catalog. Replacing
        /// a mount with identical contents still invalidates this operation context.
        pub fn verify(&self) -> Result<()> {
            ensure!(
                (self.probe)(&self.path, &self.root)? == self.mount_id,
                "3tchedFS mount instance changed"
            );
            let current = OpenOptions::new()
                .read(true)
                .custom_flags(libc::O_DIRECTORY | libc::O_NOFOLLOW)
                .open(&self.path)
                .context("reopen mount root")?;
            let original = self.root.metadata()?;
            let present = current.metadata()?;
            ensure!(
                original.dev() == present.dev() && original.ino() == present.ino(),
                "3tchedFS root changed"
            );
            ensure!(
                read_json(open_relative(&self.root, ".3tchedfs.json", false)?)? == self.metadata,
                "3tchedFS identity or catalog declaration changed"
            );
            ensure!(
                read_json(open_relative(&self.root, "view.json", false)?)? == self.view,
                "3tchedFS view changed"
            );
            Ok(())
        }
    
        /// Read only the sealed declaration nodes. The mount pins their object
        /// locator and catalog; no public state or object payload is required.
        pub fn schema(&self, plugin: &str) -> Result<PluginSchema> {
            self.verify()?;
            let hash = self.view["objects"]
                .get(plugin)
                .and_then(Value::as_str)
                .context("plugin hash absent from mounted catalog")?;
            let prefix = format!("plugins/{}", encode_component(plugin));
            let schema: PluginSchema = serde_json::from_value(read_json(open_relative(
                &self.root,
                &format!("{prefix}/schema.json"),
                false,
            )?)?)?;
            ensure!(schema.name == plugin, "mounted plugin identity mismatch");
            ensure!(
                hash == read_bounded(
                    open_relative(&self.root, &format!("{prefix}/object.hash"), false)?,
                    1024
                )?
                .trim(),
                "mounted object hash declaration mismatch"
            );
            self.verify()?;
            Ok(schema)
        }
    
        pub fn object(&self, plugin: &str) -> Result<TypedObjectBlob> {

    //! gRPC Client - For D-Bus → remote gRPC calls
    //!
    //! Allows local D-Bus services to call remote gRPC endpoints,
    //! enabling distributed operation-dbus deployments.
    
    use std::collections::HashMap;
    use std::sync::Arc;
    use std::time::Duration;
    
    use base64::Engine as _;
    use prost_types::{Struct as ProstStruct, Value as ProstValue, value::Kind as ProstKind};
    use tokio::sync::RwLock;
    use tonic::Request;

    use tracing::info;

        plugin_service_client::PluginServiceClient, state_sync_client::StateSyncClient,
    };
    
    /// Bounded response envelope for complete plugin documents and SHM state.
    /// Native chat can exceed tonic's 4 MiB default; identity admission is unchanged.
    pub const MAX_PLUGIN_STATE_RESPONSE_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
    
    
    /// Configuration for a remote gRPC endpoint
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub struct RemoteEndpoint {
        pub address: String,
        pub tls_enabled: bool,
        pub connect_timeout: Duration,
        pub request_timeout: Duration,
    }
    
    /// Caller-supplied Ghostbridge identity forwarded by an HTTP compatibility
    /// adapter into the canonical gRPC method call.
    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub struct GhostbridgeCallMetadata {
        /// Exact caller-supplied SID1 wire bytes, if this is a local identity call.
        pub sealed_id: Option<Vec<u8>>,
        /// Exact caller-supplied OIA1 wire bytes, if this is a decoy assertion call.
        pub oracle_assertion: Option<Vec<u8>>,
        /// Legacy fields retained for non-plugin Ghostbridge services.
        pub session_genesis: Option<String>,
        pub trace_id: Option<String>,
        pub wireguard_pubkey: Option<String>,
    }
    
    impl Default for RemoteEndpoint {
        fn default() -> Self {
            Self {
                address: "http://127.0.0.1:8090".to_string(),
                tls_enabled: false,
                connect_timeout: Duration::from_secs(5),
                request_timeout: Duration::from_secs(30),
            }
        }
    }
    
    /// gRPC client pool for connecting to remote Operation services
    pub struct GrpcClientPool {
        /// Map of endpoint address to channel
        channels: RwLock<HashMap<String, Channel>>,
        /// Default endpoint configuration
        default_config: RemoteEndpoint,
    }
    
    impl Default for GrpcClientPool {
        fn default() -> Self {
            Self::new()
        }
    }
    
    impl GrpcClientPool {
        pub fn new() -> Self {
            Self {
                channels: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
                default_config: RemoteEndpoint::default(),
            }
        }
    
        pub fn with_default_config(config: RemoteEndpoint) -> Self {
            Self {
                channels: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
                default_config: config,
            }
        }
    
        /// Apply transport settings (timeouts + TLS) to an endpoint.
        ///
        /// TLS is driven by the URI scheme: `https://` gets a tonic
        /// `ClientTlsConfig`. This mirrors `examples/repro_subscribe.rs`, which is
        /// the reference client path. Trust anchors, in priority order:
        ///   1. `OP_DBUS_GRPC_CA_FILE` — PEM file to pin (what op-web's run script
        ///      exports; may point at the leaf cert itself since it is its own CA).
        ///   2. Native system roots (`with_native_roots`).
        ///
        /// `OP_DBUS_GRPC_TLS_DOMAIN` overrides the SNI/verification name when the
        /// dial address is an IP or differs from the certificate SAN.
        fn configure_endpoint(
            &self,
            endpoint: Endpoint,
            addr: &str,
        ) -> Result<Endpoint, GrpcClientError> {
            let endpoint = endpoint
                .connect_timeout(self.default_config.connect_timeout)
                .timeout(self.default_config.request_timeout);
    
            if !addr.starts_with("https://") {
                return Ok(endpoint);
            }
    
            let mut tls = ClientTlsConfig::new().with_native_roots();
            if let Ok(path) = std::env::var("OP_DBUS_GRPC_CA_FILE")
                && !path.trim().is_empty()
            {
                let pem = std::fs::read(path.trim()).map_err(|e| {
                    GrpcClientError::ConnectionFailed(format!(
                        "failed to read OP_DBUS_GRPC_CA_FILE={path}: {e}"
                    ))
                })?;
                tls = tls.ca_certificate(Certificate::from_pem(pem));
            }
            if let Ok(domain) = std::env::var("OP_DBUS_GRPC_TLS_DOMAIN")
                && !domain.trim().is_empty()
            {
                tls = tls.domain_name(domain.trim().to_string());
            }
            endpoint
                .tls_config(tls)
                .map_err(|e| GrpcClientError::ConnectionFailed(format!("TLS config for {addr}: {e}")))
        }
    
        /// Get or create a channel to the specified address (supports comma-separated endpoints for load balancing)
        async fn get_channel(&self, address: &str) -> Result<Channel, GrpcClientError> {
            {
                let channels = self.channels.read().await;
                if let Some(channel) = channels.get(address) {
                    return Ok(channel.clone());
                }
            }
    
            let addrs: Vec<&str> = address
                .split(',')
                .map(|s| s.trim())
                .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
                .collect();
    
            let channel = if addrs.len() > 1 {
                // Native Tonic Load Balancing
                let endpoints = addrs
                    .into_iter()
                    .map(|addr| {
                        Endpoint::from_shared(addr.to_string())
                            .map_err(|e| {
                                GrpcClientError::ConnectionFailed(format!(
                                    "Invalid endpoint {addr}: {e}"
                                ))
                            })
                            .and_then(|e| self.configure_endpoint(e, addr))
                    })
                    .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
    
                Channel::balance_list(endpoints.into_iter())
            } else {
                // Single endpoint
                let endpoint = Endpoint::from_shared(address.to_string())
                    .map_err(|e| GrpcClientError::ConnectionFailed(e.to_string()))?;
                let endpoint = self.configure_endpoint(endpoint, address)?;
    
                endpoint
                    .connect()
                    .await
                    .map_err(|e| GrpcClientError::ConnectionFailed(e.to_string()))?
            };
    
            {
                let mut channels = self.channels.write().await;
                channels.insert(address.to_string(), channel.clone());
            }
    
            info!("Connected to remote gRPC endpoint(s): {}", address);
            Ok(channel)
        }

        a2a_routes_with_endpoint(None)
    }
    
    /// A2A discovery routes using the runtime listener endpoint for URL
    /// advertisement when config does not set a stronger override.
    pub(crate) fn a2a_routes_with_endpoint(
        endpoint: Option<AdvertisedGatewayEndpoint>,
    ) -> Router<AppState> {
        Router::new()
            .route(CATALOG_CARD_PATH, get(handle_catalog_card))
            .route(CATALOG_CARD_PREFIXED_PATH, get(handle_catalog_card))
            .route(
                &format!("/a2a/{{alias}}{WELL_KNOWN_AGENT_CARD_PATH}"),
                get(handle_alias_card),
            )
            .layer(Extension(endpoint))
    }
    
    pub fn a2a_task_route() -> Router<AppState> {
        Router::new().route("/a2a/{alias}", post(handle_alias_task))
    }

        fn write_skill(root: &std::path::Path, bundle: &str, name: &str, display: &str) {
            let dir = root.join("shared/skills").join(bundle).join(name);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).expect("mkdir skill");
            std::fs::write(
                dir.join("SKILL.md"),
                format!(
                    "---\nname: {display}\ndescription: {display} does things.\n---\n\n# {display}\n"
                ),
            )
            .expect("write manifest");
        }

            let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().expect("tmp");
            write_skill(tmp.path(), "demo", "widget", "Widget");
            write_skill(tmp.path(), "demo", "gadget", "Gadget");
            write_skill(tmp.path(), "other", "intruder", "Intruder");
    
            let mut config = config_with_published_alias("maker", true);
            config.config_path = tmp.path().join("config.toml");
            config
                .skill_bundles
                .insert("demo".to_string(), Default::default());
            config
                .skill_bundles
                .insert("other".to_string(), Default::default());
            {
                let agent = config.agents.get_mut("maker").unwrap();
                agent.skill_bundles = vec!["demo".to_string()];
                agent.a2a.exposed_skills = vec!["widget".to_string(), "intruder".to_string()];
            }
    
            let card = build_agent_card(&config, "maker").expect("card");
            // widget resolves from the declared bundle; intruder is in a bundle the
            // agent does not declare, so it is excluded even though it exists.
            let ids: Vec<&str> = card.skills.iter().map(|s| s.id.as_str()).collect();
            assert_eq!(ids, vec!["widget"]);
            assert_eq!(card.skills[0].name, "Widget");
            // Per-alias card tags carry the owning bundle.
            assert_eq!(card.skills[0].tags, vec!["demo".to_string()]);
    
            let catalog = build_catalog_card(&config);
            assert_eq!(catalog.skills.len(), 1);
            assert_eq!(catalog.skills[0].id, "maker/widget");
            // The catalog appends the owning alias on top of the resolved bundle
            // tag rather than replacing it, so both survive.
            assert_eq!(
                catalog.skills[0].tags,
                vec!["demo".to_string(), "maker".to_string()]
            );
        }

    fn test_catalog() -> Catalog {
        Catalog::from_entries(vec![PluginEntry {
            id: "demo.plugin".to_string(),
            name: "Demo".to_string(),
            version: "1.0.0".to_string(),
            schema_hash: "schema-abc".to_string(),
            tags: vec!["demo".to_string()],
            methods: vec![PluginMethod {
                name: "Ping".to_string(),
            }],
            ..Default::default()
        }])
        .expect("valid catalog")
    }
    
    fn set_property_op(member: &str, value: serde_json::Value) -> CoreMutation {
        CoreMutation {
            plugin_id: "demo.plugin".to_string(),
            object_path: "/demo/obj".to_string(),
            operation: CoreOperation::SetProperty,
            member_name: member.to_string(),
            value,
            actor_id: "tester".to_string(),
            capability_id: String::new(),
            idempotency_key: String::new(),
        }
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn mutate_then_get_state_roundtrip() {
        let core = BridgeCore::new(test_catalog());
        let outcome = core
            .mutate(set_property_op("volume", serde_json::json!(7)))
            .expect("mutation accepted");
        assert_eq!(outcome.event.event_id, 1);
    
        let (map, hash) = core
            .get_object("demo.plugin", "/demo/obj")
            .expect("object present");
        assert_eq!(map.get("volume"), Some(&serde_json::json!(7)));
        assert_eq!(hash, outcome.event.result_effective_hash);
        assert_eq!(core.at_event_id(), 1);
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn verify_chain_recomputes_journal() {
        let core = BridgeCore::new(test_catalog());
        for i in 0..5 {
            core.mutate(set_property_op(&format!("key{i}"), serde_json::json!(i)))
                .expect("mutation accepted");
        }
    
        let checked = core.journal().verify(0, 0);
        assert!(checked.valid, "errors: {:?}", checked.errors);
        assert_eq!(checked.events_verified, 5);
        assert!(checked.errors.is_empty());
    
        // Sub-range recompute holds too.
        let sub = core.journal().verify(2, 4);
        assert!(sub.valid, "errors: {:?}", sub.errors);
        assert_eq!(sub.events_verified, 3);
    
        // Linkage: genesis has no predecessor; every other event links back.
        let events = core.journal().range(0, 0);
        assert_eq!(events.len(), 5);
        assert!(events[0].prev_hash.is_empty());
        for pair in events.windows(2) {
            assert_eq!(pair[1].prev_hash, pair[0].event_hash);
        }
    }

        let catalog = test_catalog();
        let expected = catalog.hash().to_string();
        let core = BridgeCore::new(catalog);
    
        let mut live = core.subscribe_state();
        core.mutate(set_property_op("volume", serde_json::json!(7)))
            .expect("mutation accepted");
        let frame = live.try_recv().expect("exactly one frame published");
        assert_eq!(frame.catalog_hash, expected);
        assert_eq!(frame.schema_hash, "schema-abc");
        assert_eq!(frame.event_id, 1);
        assert!(live.try_recv().is_err(), "no second frame");
    
        // Hydration frames carry it too.
        let initial = core.initial_frames();
        assert_eq!(initial.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(initial[0].catalog_hash, expected);

    impl BridgeCore {
        /// A fresh core over `catalog`, with empty state, journal and routes.
        pub fn new(catalog: Catalog) -> Self {
            // Depth 1024: slow subscribers lag (and skip) rather than block writers.
            let (state_tx, _) = broadcast::channel(1024);
            let (event_tx, _) = broadcast::channel(1024);
            Self {
                inner: Arc::new(BridgeCoreInner {
                    commit: Mutex::new(()),
                    catalog,
                    store: StateStore::new(),
                    journal: Journal::new(),
                    router: Router::new(),
                    state_tx,
                    event_tx,
                }),
            }
        }
    
        /// The route source of truth.
        pub fn catalog(&self) -> &Catalog {
            &self.inner.catalog
        }
    
        /// The object state store.
        pub fn store(&self) -> &StateStore {
            &self.inner.store
        }
    
        /// The hash-chained audit journal.
        pub fn journal(&self) -> &Journal {
            &self.inner.journal
        }
    
        /// The method router.
        pub fn router(&self) -> &Router {
            &self.inner.router
        }
    
        /// Register (or replace) one method handler.
        pub fn register_handler(
            &self,
            plugin_id: impl Into<String>,
            method: impl Into<String>,
            handler: Handler,
        ) {
            self.inner.router.register(plugin_id, method, handler);
        }
    
        /// Subscribe to live [`StateChange`] frames.
        pub fn subscribe_state(&self) -> broadcast::Receiver<StateChange> {
            self.inner.state_tx.subscribe()
        }
    
        /// Subscribe to live [`ChainEvent`]s.
        pub fn subscribe_events(&self) -> broadcast::Receiver<ChainEvent> {
            self.inner.event_tx.subscribe()
        }
    
        /// Latest journaled event id, or 0 when the journal is empty.
        pub fn at_event_id(&self) -> u64 {
            self.inner.journal.tip().map(|t| t.event_id).unwrap_or(0)
        }
    
        /// Whole-object read plus its effective hash.
        pub fn get_object(
            &self,
            plugin_id: &str,
            object_path: &str,
        ) -> Option<(serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>, String)> {
            let _commit = self.inner.commit.lock().expect("commit lock poisoned");
            self.inner.store.get_object(plugin_id, object_path)
        }
    
        /// Read state, hash and resume cursor from the same committed snapshot.
        pub fn get_object_snapshot(
            &self,
            plugin_id: &str,
            object_path: &str,
        ) -> Option<(serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>, String, u64)> {
            let _commit = self.inner.commit.lock().expect("commit lock poisoned");
            let (state, hash) = self.inner.store.get_object(plugin_id, object_path)?;
            let event_id = self
                .inner
                .journal
                .tip()
                .map(|event| event.event_id)
                .unwrap_or(0);
            Some((state, hash, event_id))
        }
    
        /// Read a property after any in-progress atomic state batch commits.
        pub fn get_property(
            &self,
            plugin_id: &str,
            object_path: &str,
            member: &str,
        ) -> Option<serde_json::Value> {
            let _commit = self.inner.commit.lock().expect("commit lock poisoned");
            self.inner.store.get_member(plugin_id, object_path, member)
        }
    
        /// Capture hydration and its live receiver at one commit boundary.
        pub(crate) fn state_subscription(
            &self,
            include_state: bool,
            include_schema: bool,
        ) -> (
            Vec<StateChange>,
            Vec<StateChange>,
            broadcast::Receiver<StateChange>,
        ) {
            let _commit = self.inner.commit.lock().expect("commit lock poisoned");
            let live = self.subscribe_state();
            let initial = if include_state {
                self.initial_frames_locked()
            } else {
                Vec::new()
            };
            let schemas = if include_schema {
                self.schema_frames_locked()
            } else {
                Vec::new()
            };
            (initial, schemas, live)
        }
    
        /// History ends before any event that can arrive on the returned receiver.
        pub(crate) fn event_subscription(

            let schema: PluginSchema = serde_json::from_value(read_json(open_relative(

                false,
            )?)?)?;
            ensure!(schema.name == plugin, "mounted plugin identity mismatch");
            ensure!(

                    1024

                .trim(),
                "mounted object hash declaration mismatch"
            );
            self.verify()?;
            Ok(schema)
        }
    
        pub fn object(&self, plugin: &str) -> Result<TypedObjectBlob> {
            self.verify()?;
            let hash = self.view["objects"]
                .get(plugin)
                .context("plugin absent from mounted catalog")?;
            let prefix = format!("plugins/{}", encode_component(plugin));
            let object: TypedObjectBlob = serde_json::from_value(read_json(open_relative(
                &self.root,
                &format!("{prefix}/object.blob.json"),
                false,
            )?)?)?;
            ensure!(
                object.plugin_id == plugin && object.schema.name == plugin,
                "mounted plugin identity mismatch"
            );
            ensure!(
                hash.as_str()
                    == Some(
                        read_bounded(
                            open_relative(&self.root, &format!("{prefix}/object.hash"), false)?,
                            1024
                        )?
                        .trim()
                    ),
                "mounted object hash declaration mismatch"
            );
            ensure!(
                read_json(open_relative(
                    &self.root,
                    &format!("{prefix}/schema.json"),
                    false
                )?)? == serde_json::to_value(&object.schema)?,
                "mounted schema differs from pinned object"
            );
            self.verify()?;
            Ok(object)
        }
    
        pub fn plugins(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
            self.verify()?;
            let plugins = self.view["objects"]
                .as_object()
                .context("missing catalog")?
                .keys()
                .cloned()
                .collect();
            self.verify()?;
            Ok(plugins)
        }
    
        pub fn view_id(&self) -> Result<&str> {
            self.metadata["view_id"]

                &self.root,
                &format!("plugins/{}/value.json", encode_component(plugin)),
                false,
            )?)?;
            self.verify()?;
            Ok(state)
        }
