    //! Thin tonic server: the three core services plus gRPC reflection.
    
    use crate::core::BridgeCore;
    use crate::proto::event_chain_service_server::EventChainServiceServer;
    use crate::proto::plugin_service_server::PluginServiceServer;
    use crate::proto::state_sync_server::StateSyncServer;
    use crate::proto::FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET;
    use crate::service::BridgeService;
    use std::net::SocketAddr;
    use tokio::net::TcpListener;
    use tokio_stream::wrappers::TcpListenerStream;
    
    /// Serve `StateSync`, `PluginService` and `EventChainService` (plus
    /// reflection) on `addr`. Runs until the server errors.
    pub async fn serve(addr: SocketAddr, core: BridgeCore) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        serve_with_listener(TcpListener::bind(addr).await?, core).await
    }
    
    /// Serve on an already bound listener, retaining ownership of its address.
    pub async fn serve_with_listener(listener: TcpListener, core: BridgeCore) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let service = BridgeService::new(core);
        let reflection = tonic_reflection::server::Builder::configure()
            .register_encoded_file_descriptor_set(FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET)
            .build_v1()?;
        tonic::transport::Server::builder()
            .add_service(StateSyncServer::new(service.clone()))
            .add_service(PluginServiceServer::new(service.clone()))
            .add_service(EventChainServiceServer::new(service))
            .add_service(reflection)
            .serve_with_incoming(TcpListenerStream::new(listener))
            .await?;
        Ok(())
    }
    //! Exact method grant checks for already verified SID1 identities.
    //! The caller must check compiled handler compatibility and revalidate before
    //! dispatch; this gate does not execute the method or validate arguments.
    
    use crate::identity_receiver::VerifiedSid1;
    use op_state_store::{MethodDecl, PluginSchema};
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    
    /// Require the sealed method's exact capability and the principal's exact grant.
    /// The grant document must come from the protected grant projection, never a caller.
    pub(crate) fn require_method_grant(
        identity: &VerifiedSid1,
        catalog_dir: &Path,
        plugin_id: &str,
        canonical_method: &str,
        requested_capability: Option<&str>,
        grants: &serde_json::Value,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<(MethodDecl, String)> {
        let pinned = crate::catalog::Catalog::sealed_plugin(catalog_dir, plugin_id)?;
        let schema: PluginSchema = serde_json::from_value(
            pinned
                .schema
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("sealed plugin schema is unavailable"))?,
        )?;
        let declaration = schema
            .methods
            .get(canonical_method)
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("sealed method is unavailable"))?;
        let required = declaration
            .required_capability
            .as_deref()
            .map(str::trim)
            .filter(|capability| !capability.is_empty())
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("sealed method capability is unavailable"))?;
        let claims = identity.claims();
        anyhow::ensure!(
            !claims.principal_id.is_empty() && !claims.session_id.is_empty(),
            "verified identity is incomplete"
        );
        anyhow::ensure!(
            claims.expires_at == 0 || claims.expires_at > chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
            "verified identity has expired"
        );
        anyhow::ensure!(
            requested_capability == Some(required),
            "requested capability does not match the sealed method"
        );
        anyhow::ensure!(
            crate::grant_document::capabilities_for_principal(grants, &claims.principal_id)
                .contains(required),
            "principal lacks the required capability"
        );
        Ok((declaration.clone(), pinned.schema_hash))
    }

            let grants: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(grants_path)?)?;

    //! TLS door for HTTP callers (used by `op-web`): PEM identity plus an

    //! tonic's `Identity` hides the key and its HTTP/1 transport drops upgraded
    //! connections, so the TCP door configures rustls from the same PEM pair.
    
    use std::convert::Infallible;
    use std::io::BufReader;
    use std::sync::Arc;
    use std::time::Duration;
    
    use axum::body::Body;
    use axum::extract::connect_info::ConnectInfo;
    use axum::Router;
    use hyper::body::Incoming;
    use hyper_util::rt::{TokioExecutor, TokioIo, TokioTimer};
    use hyper_util::server::conn::auto::Builder;
    use tokio_rustls::rustls;
    use tokio_rustls::TlsAcceptor;
    use tower::Service;
    
    /// Keep the selected PEM pair available to the upgrade-capable TCP server.
    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub struct PemIdentity {
        cert: Vec<u8>,
        key: Vec<u8>,
    }
    
    impl std::fmt::Debug for PemIdentity {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str("PemIdentity([redacted])")
        }
    }
    
    impl PemIdentity {
        pub fn from_pem(cert: impl AsRef<[u8]>, key: impl AsRef<[u8]>) -> Self {
            Self {
                cert: cert.as_ref().to_vec(),
                key: key.as_ref().to_vec(),
            }
        }
    
        pub fn server_config(&self) -> anyhow::Result<Arc<rustls::ServerConfig>> {
            let certs = rustls_pemfile::certs(&mut BufReader::new(self.cert.as_slice()))
                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
            anyhow::ensure!(!certs.is_empty(), "TCP TLS certificate chain is empty");
            let key = rustls_pemfile::private_key(&mut BufReader::new(self.key.as_slice()))?
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("TCP TLS private key is missing"))?;
            let mut config = rustls::ServerConfig::builder_with_provider(Arc::new(
                rustls::crypto::aws_lc_rs::default_provider(),
            ))
            .with_safe_default_protocol_versions()?
            .with_no_client_auth()
            .with_single_cert(certs, key)?;
            config.alpn_protocols = vec![b"h2".to_vec(), b"http/1.1".to_vec()];
            Ok(Arc::new(config))
        }
    }
    
    /// Serve `app` over TLS on `listener`, allowing HTTP/1 upgrades
    /// (websockets). Runs until the listener errors.
    pub async fn serve_upgradeable_tcp(
        listener: tokio::net::TcpListener,
        tls: Arc<rustls::ServerConfig>,
        app: Router,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        const MAX_CONNECTIONS: usize = 512;
        let permits = Arc::new(tokio::sync::Semaphore::new(MAX_CONNECTIONS));
        let acceptor = TlsAcceptor::from(tls);
        loop {
            let permit = permits.clone().acquire_owned().await?;
            let (stream, peer) = match listener.accept().await {
                Ok(accepted) => accepted,
                Err(error) => {
                    tracing::warn!(%error, "TCP door accept failed");
                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)).await;
                    continue;
                }
            };
            let acceptor = acceptor.clone();
            let app = app.clone();
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                let permit = Arc::new(permit);
                let tls =
                    match tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), acceptor.accept(stream)).await {
                        Ok(Ok(tls)) => tls,
                        _ => return,
                    };
                let service = hyper::service::service_fn(move |request: hyper::Request<Incoming>| {
                    let mut app = app.clone();
                    let permit = permit.clone();
                    async move {
                        let mut request = request.map(Body::new);
                        request.extensions_mut().insert(ConnectInfo(peer));
                        request.extensions_mut().insert(permit);
                        let response = app.call(request).await?;
                        Ok::<_, Infallible>(response)
                    }
                });
                let mut builder = Builder::new(TokioExecutor::new());
                builder
                    .http1()
                    .timer(TokioTimer::new())
                    .header_read_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10));
                if let Err(error) = builder
                    .serve_connection_with_upgrades(TokioIo::new(tls), service)
                    .await
                {
                    tracing::debug!(%error, "TCP door connection closed");
                }
            });
        }
    }

    //! Plugin catalog: the route source of truth.
    //!
    //! Accepted JSON shapes (all decode to the same catalog):
    //! - `{ "plugins": [ <entry>, ... ] }`
    //! - `{ "entries": [ <entry>, ... ] }`
    //! - `[ <entry>, ... ]`

        Duplicate(String),
    }

    where
        D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,
    {
        #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
        #[serde(untagged)]
        enum M {
            Named(PluginMethod),
            Plain(String),
        }
        Ok(Vec::<M>::deserialize(d)?
            .into_iter()
            .map(|m| match m {
                M::Named(p) => p,
                M::Plain(s) => PluginMethod::from(s),
            })
            .collect())
    }

    fn read_sealed_entry(dir: &Path, id: &str, schema_hash: &str) -> anyhow::Result<PluginEntry> {
        let schema = op_blob::catalog::read_plugin_state_store_schema(dir, id)
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid sealed plugin {id}"))?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            schema_hash.len() == 64 && schema_hash.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()),
            "invalid schema hash for {id}"
        );
        let bytes = std::fs::read(dir.join(format!("{id}.{}.blob", &schema_hash[..16])))?;
        let blob = op_blob::BlobRef::from_manifest_pinned(&bytes, schema_hash)
            .map_err(|error| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid sealed plugin {id}: {error}"))?;
        let pinned_schema = blob
            .state_store_schema()
            .map_err(|error| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid sealed plugin {id}: {error}"))?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            serde_json::to_value(&schema)? == serde_json::to_value(&pinned_schema)?,
            "sealed plugin {id} changed during read"
        );
        let raw_schema = serde_json::from_str(blob.schema_json())?;
        let mut methods: Vec<_> = schema
            .methods
            .keys()
            .cloned()
            .map(PluginMethod::from)
            .collect();
        methods.sort_by(|a, b| a.name.cmp(&b.name));
        Ok(PluginEntry {
            id: id.to_owned(),
            name: schema.name,
            version: schema.version,
            description: schema.description,
            dbus_path: format!("/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/{id}"),
            tags: schema.tags,
            schema_hash: schema_hash.to_owned(),
            schema: Some(raw_schema),
            sealed_schema_json: Some(blob.schema_json().to_owned()),
            methods,
            ..Default::default()
        })
    }

    //!
    //! Handlers are pure value-in/value-out functions over JSON values. Async or
    //! D-Bus-backed behavior plugs in behind [`BridgeCore`](crate::core::BridgeCore)
    //! call sites, not inside the router.
    
    use std::collections::HashMap;
    use std::sync::{Arc, RwLock};
    
    /// A synchronous value-in/value-out method handler.
    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub struct Handler(
        Arc<dyn Fn(&[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<serde_json::Value, RouterError> + Send + Sync>,
    );
    
    impl Handler {
        /// Wrap a plain closure as a handler.
        pub fn new<F>(f: F) -> Self
        where
            F: Fn(&[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<serde_json::Value, RouterError>
                + Send
                + Sync
                + 'static,
        {
            Self(Arc::new(f))
        }
    
        /// Run the handler.
        pub fn call(&self, args: &[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<serde_json::Value, RouterError> {
            (self.0)(args)
        }
    }
    
    impl<F> From<F> for Handler
    where
        F: Fn(&[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<serde_json::Value, RouterError> + Send + Sync + 'static,
    {
        fn from(f: F) -> Self {
            Self::new(f)
        }
    }
    
    impl std::fmt::Debug for Handler {
        fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
            f.write_str("Handler(..)")
        }
    }
    
    /// Router failure: unknown route, or a handler that returned an error.
    #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
    pub enum RouterError {
        /// No route table entry for this plugin at all.
        #[error("unknown plugin: {0}")]
        UnknownPlugin(String),
        /// Plugin is routed, but this method is not.
        #[error("unknown method '{method}' for plugin '{plugin_id}'")]
        UnknownMethod { plugin_id: String, method: String },
        /// The handler ran and failed.
        #[error("handler for '{plugin_id}.{method}' failed: {message}")]
        HandlerFailed {
            plugin_id: String,
            method: String,
            message: String,
        },
    }
    
    /// Synchronous `(plugin_id, method)` dispatch table. Cheap to clone.
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
    pub struct Router {
        routes: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, HashMap<String, Handler>>>>,
    }
    
    impl Router {
        /// An empty router.
        pub fn new() -> Self {
            Self::default()
        }
    
        /// Register (or replace) the handler for one route.
        pub fn register(
            &self,
            plugin_id: impl Into<String>,
            method: impl Into<String>,
            handler: Handler,
        ) {
            self.routes
                .write()
                .expect("router lock poisoned")
                .entry(plugin_id.into())
                .or_default()
                .insert(method.into(), handler);
        }
    
        /// Is a handler registered for this route?
        pub fn has(&self, plugin_id: &str, method: &str) -> bool {
            self.routes
                .read()
                .expect("router lock poisoned")
                .get(plugin_id)
                .is_some_and(|methods| methods.contains_key(method))
        }
    
        /// Dispatch one call. The table lock is released before the handler runs.
        pub fn call(
            &self,
            plugin_id: &str,
            method: &str,
            args: &[serde_json::Value],
        ) -> Result<serde_json::Value, RouterError> {
            let handler = {
                let routes = self.routes.read().expect("router lock poisoned");
                let methods = routes
                    .get(plugin_id)
                    .ok_or_else(|| RouterError::UnknownPlugin(plugin_id.to_string()))?;
                methods
                    .get(method)
                    .cloned()
                    .ok_or_else(|| RouterError::UnknownMethod {
                        plugin_id: plugin_id.to_string(),
                        method: method.to_string(),
                    })?
            };
            handler.call(args).map_err(|err| match err {
                // A handler that returns routing errors is confused; normalize.
                RouterError::HandlerFailed { .. } => err,
                other => RouterError::HandlerFailed {
                    plugin_id: plugin_id.to_string(),
                    method: method.to_string(),
                    message: other.to_string(),
                },
            })
        }
    }

        async fn call_method(
            &self,
            request: Request<CallMethodRequest>,
        ) -> Result<Response<CallMethodResponse>, Status> {
            let req = request.into_inner();
            // Routes key on (plugin, method); interface_name is informational.
            let args: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
                req.arguments.iter().map(proto_value_to_json).collect();
            let op = CoreMutation {
                plugin_id: req.plugin_id.clone(),
                object_path: req.object_path.clone(),
                operation: CoreOperation::CallMethod,
                member_name: req.method_name.clone(),
                value: serde_json::Value::Array(args),
                actor_id: req.actor_id.clone(),
                capability_id: req.capability_id.clone(),
                idempotency_key: String::new(),
            };
            match self.core.mutate(op) {
                Ok(outcome) => Ok(Response::new(CallMethodResponse {
                    success: true,
                    result: outcome.result.as_ref().map(json_to_proto_value),
                    event_id: outcome.event.event_id,
                    event_hash: outcome.event.event_hash,
                    error: None,
                })),
                Err(rejection) => Ok(Response::new(CallMethodResponse {
                    success: false,
                    result: None,
                    event_id: 0,
                    event_hash: String::new(),
                    error: Some(mutation_error(rejection.code, rejection.message)),
                })),
            }
        }

            let req = request.into_inner();
            if self.core.catalog().plugin(&req.plugin_id).is_none() {
                return Err(Status::not_found(format!(
                    "unknown plugin '{}'",
                    req.plugin_id
                )));
            }
            match self.core.get_property(
                &req.plugin_id,
                &req.object_path,
                &req.property_name,
            ) {
                Some(value) => Ok(Response::new(GetPropertyResponse {
                    value: Some(json_to_proto_value(&value)),
                    read_only: false,
                })),
                None => Err(Status::not_found(format!(
                    "no property '{}' on '{}:{}'",
                    req.property_name, req.plugin_id, req.object_path
                ))),
            }
        }

    //! SID1 receiver over the committed private identity projection.
    //! This does not admit an RPC, evaluate grants, or handle OIA1 assertions.
    
    use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    
    use base64::Engine as _;
    use op_identity::sealed_id::SealedId;
    use op_plugins::state_plugins::identity_sled::{ContainerIdentitySled, IdentitySledState};
    use op_state_store::FieldSchema;
    use serde::Deserialize;
    
    use crate::catalog::Catalog;
    
    /// SID1 verified against committed state, its binding and the active principal registry.
    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub struct VerifiedSid1(SealedId);
    
    pub(crate) struct BoundSid1(SealedId);
    
    impl BoundSid1 {
        pub(crate) fn claims(&self) -> &SealedId {
            &self.0
        }
    }
    
    impl std::fmt::Debug for VerifiedSid1 {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str("VerifiedSid1([redacted])")
        }
    }
    
    impl VerifiedSid1 {
        pub fn claims(&self) -> &SealedId {
            &self.0
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct CompiledIdentityContract {
        version: String,
        fields: HashMap<String, FieldSchema>,
    }
    
    fn pinned_identity(dir: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<crate::catalog::PluginEntry> {
        let pinned = Catalog::sealed_plugin(dir, "identity_sled")?;
        let schema: op_state_store::PluginSchema = serde_json::from_value(
            pinned
                .schema
                .clone()
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("sealed identity schema absent"))?,
        )?;
        let compiled: CompiledIdentityContract = serde_json::from_str(include_str!(concat!(
            env!("OUT_DIR"),
            "/identity_state_contract.json"
        )))?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            schema.version == compiled.version && schema.fields == compiled.fields,
            "compiled and sealed identity state contracts differ"
        );
        Ok(pinned)
    }
    
    fn committed_session(
        catalog_dir: &Path,
        state_dir: &str,
        session_id: &str,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<Option<ContainerIdentitySled>> {
        let before = pinned_identity(catalog_dir)?;
        let bytes =
            op_core::projection_shm::read_credential_projection_bytes_in(state_dir, "identity_sled")?
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("committed identity credential projection is absent"))?;
        let after = pinned_identity(catalog_dir)?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            before.schema_hash == after.schema_hash
                && before.sealed_schema_json == after.sealed_schema_json,
            "identity plugin seal changed during credential state access"
        );
        let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            value.get("sleds").is_some_and(serde_json::Value::is_array),
            "identity sleds missing"
        );
        anyhow::ensure!(
            value.get("events").is_some_and(serde_json::Value::is_array),
            "identity events missing"
        );
        let state: IdentitySledState = serde_json::from_value(value)?;
        let mut ids = HashSet::new();
        for sled in &state.sleds {
            anyhow::ensure!(
                ids.insert(sled.session_id.as_str()),
                "duplicate identity in SHM"
            );
            crate::identity_binding::validate_sled(sled)?;
        }
        let mut events = HashSet::new();
        for event in &state.events {
            anyhow::ensure!(
                events.insert((event.session_id.as_str(), event.seq)),
                "duplicate identity event in SHM"
            );
        }
        Ok(state
            .sleds
            .into_iter()
            .find(|sled| sled.session_id == session_id))
    }
    
    pub(crate) fn verify_in(
        catalog_dir: &Path,
        state_dir: &str,
        wire: &[u8],
        transport: &str,
        now: i64,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<BoundSid1> {
        let claims =
            crate::sid1_checks::parse_for_transport(wire, transport).map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?;
        let sled = committed_session(catalog_dir, state_dir, &claims.session_id)?
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("sealed identity session was not found"))?;
        let claims = crate::sid1_checks::match_bound_session(wire, &sled, transport, now)
            .map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?;
        Ok(BoundSid1(claims))
    }

    //! Bounded execution of the binary-backed filesystem surface.
    //!
    //! The child owns a new process group. Its leader remains unreaped until group
    //! cleanup is complete, so a group signal cannot race reuse of the leader PID.
    //! Both pipes are drained on this thread; no reader can outlive the mount job.
    
    use crate::fuse_buffers::{Budget, Buffer, DOCUMENT_LIMIT};
    use std::io::{self, Read};
    use std::os::fd::{AsRawFd, RawFd};
    use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;
    use std::path::Path;
    use std::process::{Child, Command, ExitStatus, Stdio};
    use std::sync::{
        Arc,
        atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering},
    };
    use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
    
    const POLL_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(50);
    const READ_CHUNK: usize = 8192;
    
    /// Discovery uses the same bounded child lifetime as mounted execution,
    /// without depending on the FUSE engine or importing it into read examples.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn capture_surface(binary: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> anyhow::Result<String> {
        capture_surface_with_config(binary, args, None)
    }
    
    pub(crate) fn capture_surface_with_config(
        binary: &Path,
        args: &[&str],
        config_dir: Option<&Path>,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<String> {
        let budget = Arc::new(Budget::default());
        let cancelled = AtomicBool::new(false);
        let mut command = Command::new(binary);
        if let Some(config_dir) = config_dir {
            anyhow::ensure!(config_dir.is_absolute(), "capture config directory must be absolute");
            command.env_clear()
                .env("PATH", "/usr/bin:/bin")
                .env("HOME", config_dir.join("home"));
            command.arg("--config-dir").arg(config_dir);
        }
        command
            .args(args)
            .env("NO_COLOR", "1")
            .env("CLICOLOR", "0")
            .env("TERM", "dumb")
            .env("LANGUAGE", "en")
            .env("LC_ALL", "C")
            .env("LANG", "C");
        let output = run(
            &mut command,
            &budget,
            &cancelled,
            Limits {
                timeout: Duration::from_secs(10),
                output: 4 * 1024 * 1024,
            },
        )?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            output.status.success(),
            "{} {:?} exited with {}: {}",
            binary.display(),
            args,
            output.status,
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr.bytes)
        );
        Ok(std::str::from_utf8(&output.stdout.bytes)?.to_owned())
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
    pub(super) struct Limits {
        pub(super) timeout: Duration,
        /// Combined stdout and stderr length, additionally capped by DOCUMENT_LIMIT.
        pub(super) output: usize,
    }
    
    impl Default for Limits {
        fn default() -> Self {
            Self {
                timeout: Duration::from_secs(600),
                output: DOCUMENT_LIMIT,
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub(super) struct Output {
        pub(super) stdout: Buffer,
        pub(super) stderr: Buffer,
        pub(super) status: ExitStatus,
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
    pub enum Error {
        #[error("upstream execution was not started (errno {0})")]
        NotStarted(i32),
        #[error("upstream process could not be spawned: {0}")]
        Spawn(io::Error),
        #[error("upstream process I/O failed: {0}; outcome unknown, no automatic retry")]
        Io(#[from] io::Error),
        #[error(
            "upstream process exceeded its output or memory budget (errno {0}); outcome unknown, no automatic retry"
        )]
        Resource(i32),
        #[error("upstream process timed out; outcome unknown, no automatic retry")]
        Timeout,
        #[error("upstream process was cancelled; outcome unknown, no automatic retry")]
        Cancelled,
        #[error("threetched output is not UTF-8; outcome unknown, no automatic retry")]
        InvalidUtf8,
    }
    
    impl Error {
        pub fn stage(&self) -> &'static str {
            match self {
                Self::NotStarted(_) => "admission",
                Self::Spawn(_) => "transport",
                _ => "outcome_unknown",
            }
        }
    
        pub fn errno(&self) -> i32 {
            match self {
                Self::NotStarted(_) => libc::EBUSY,
                _ => libc::EIO,
            }
        }
    }

    //! Bind an OIA1 assertion to an existing, committed SID1 session.
    //! This partial receiver never mints identity and does not dispatch requests.
    
    use std::net::SocketAddr;
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    use std::sync::Arc;
    
    use crate::identity_receiver::VerifiedSid1;
    use crate::oracle_assertion::AssertionValidator;
    
    /// An assertion and its existing bound SID1 session. Browser-assigned oracle
    /// proofs are not supported by this receiver and fail closed.
    pub struct VerifiedOracle {
        identity: VerifiedSid1,
        assertion_expires_at: i64,
    }
    
    impl VerifiedOracle {
        pub fn identity(&self) -> &VerifiedSid1 {
            &self.identity
        }
        pub fn assertion_expires_at(&self) -> i64 {
            self.assertion_expires_at
        }
    
        async fn revalidate_in(
            &self,
            catalog_dir: &Path,
            state_dir: &str,
            now: i64,
        ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
            anyhow::ensure!(self.assertion_expires_at > now, "assertion has expired");
            let expected = self.identity.claims().clone();
            let key = expected.wireguard_pubkey.clone();
            let catalog_dir = catalog_dir.to_owned();
            let state_dir = state_dir.to_owned();
            let bound = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
                crate::identity_receiver::bound_session_for_key_in(&catalog_dir, &state_dir, &key, now)
            })
            .await??;
            let current = crate::identity_receiver::verify_bound_registry(bound).await?;
            let completed_at = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp();
            anyhow::ensure!(
                self.assertion_expires_at > completed_at,
                "assertion expired during revalidation"
            );
            anyhow::ensure!(
                current.claims().expires_at == 0 || current.claims().expires_at > completed_at,
                "identity expired during revalidation"
            );
            anyhow::ensure!(
                current.claims() == &expected,
                "assertion identity changed after verification"
            );
            Ok(())
        }
    
        /// Recheck the committed identity and active principal without replaying or
        /// reconstructing the consumed assertion. Call before backend effects and
        /// while holding long-lived subscriptions.
        pub async fn revalidate(&self) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
            let catalog_dir = std::env::var_os("OP_BLOB_CATALOG_DIR")
                .map(PathBuf::from)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(op_blob::catalog::DEFAULT_SHM_DIR));
            let state_dir = op_core::projection_shm::shm_state_dir();
            self.revalidate_in(&catalog_dir, &state_dir, chrono::Utc::now().timestamp())
                .await
        }
    }
    
    impl std::fmt::Debug for VerifiedOracle {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str("VerifiedOracle([redacted])")
        }
    }
    
    async fn verify_in(
        validator: Arc<AssertionValidator>,
        wire: &[u8],
        source: Option<SocketAddr>,
        catalog_dir: &Path,
        state_dir: &str,
        now: i64,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<VerifiedOracle> {
        let assertion_wire = wire.to_vec();
        let validator_for_check = validator.clone();
        let pending = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
            validator_for_check.validate_pending_with_bootstrap(&assertion_wire, source, now, false)
        })
        .await??;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            pending.bound_oracle().is_none(),
            "assigned browser oracle is not supported by this receiver"
        );
        let assertion = pending.identity().clone();
        let key = assertion.human_pubkey.clone();
        let catalog_dir = catalog_dir.to_owned();
        let state_dir = state_dir.to_owned();
        let bound = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
            crate::identity_receiver::bound_session_for_key_in(&catalog_dir, &state_dir, &key, now)
        })
        .await??;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            bound.claims().principal_id == assertion.principal_id
                && bound.claims().wireguard_pubkey == assertion.human_pubkey,
            "assertion does not match the committed identity"
        );
        let identity = crate::identity_receiver::verify_bound_registry(bound).await?;
        let completed_at = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp();
        anyhow::ensure!(
            assertion.expires_at > completed_at,
            "assertion expired during verification"
        );
        anyhow::ensure!(
            identity.claims().expires_at == 0 || identity.claims().expires_at > completed_at,
            "identity expired during verification"
        );
        let validator_for_consume = validator.clone();
        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || validator_for_consume.consume_pending(pending)).await??;
        Ok(VerifiedOracle {
            identity,
            assertion_expires_at: assertion.expires_at,
        })
    }
    
    /// Validate an OIA1 against the configured validator and an existing SID1.
    /// `source` must be derived from the accepted transport, never caller metadata.
    /// The caller must enforce grants, compiled handler compatibility, argument

    ) -> Result<(), GrpcClientError> {

    /// Write exactly one identity credential (SID1 or OIA1) into gRPC metadata.
    /// Ported from the legacy interceptor helper; the client keeps no second copy
    /// of the wire bytes beyond the authored credential it was given.
    fn insert_identity_metadata<T>(
        request: &mut Request<T>,
        sealed_id: Option<&[u8]>,
        oracle_assertion: Option<&[u8]>,
        capability_id: Option<&str>,
    ) -> Result<(), GrpcClientError> {
        let valid_wire =
            |wire: &[u8], magic: &[u8; 4]| wire.len() <= 16 * 1024 && wire.starts_with(magic);
        match (sealed_id, oracle_assertion) {
            (Some(_), Some(_)) => {
                return Err(GrpcClientError::RequestFailed(
                    "multiple identity credentials".into(),
                ));
            }
            (None, None) => {
                return Err(GrpcClientError::RequestFailed(
                    "missing identity credential".into(),
                ));
            }
            (Some(wire), None) => {
                if !valid_wire(wire, b"SID1") {
                    return Err(GrpcClientError::RequestFailed(
                        "invalid SID1 credential".into(),
                    ));
                }
                request.metadata_mut().insert_bin(
                    op_identity::sealed_id::HTTP_HEADER_NAME,
                    MetadataValue::from_bytes(wire),
                );
            }
            (None, Some(wire)) => {
                if !valid_wire(wire, b"OIA1") {
                    return Err(GrpcClientError::RequestFailed(
                        "invalid OIA1 credential".into(),
                    ));
                }
                request.metadata_mut().insert_bin(
                    "x-oracle-identity-assertion-bin",
                    MetadataValue::from_bytes(wire),
                );
            }
        }
        if let Some(capability_id) = capability_id {
            if capability_id.is_empty() {
                return Err(GrpcClientError::RequestFailed(
                    "capability metadata cannot be empty".into(),
                ));
            }
            request.metadata_mut().insert(
                "x-opdbus-capability",
                MetadataValue::try_from(capability_id).map_err(|error| {
                    GrpcClientError::RequestFailed(format!("invalid capability metadata: {error}"))
                })?,
            );
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    //!
    //! Every accepted mutation appends exactly one journal event and publishes
    //! exactly one [`StateChange`](crate::proto::StateChange) frame. Rejected
    //! mutations journal nothing. [`Journal::verify`] recomputes the chain, so

    /// Current wall-clock time as a protobuf Timestamp.
    pub fn now_timestamp() -> Timestamp {
        let elapsed = SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
            .unwrap_or_default();
        Timestamp {
            seconds: elapsed.as_secs() as i64,
            nanos: elapsed.subsec_nanos() as i32,
        }
    }
    
    /// Canonical JSON bytes for hashing (`serde_json::Map` is a BTreeMap, so key
    /// order is stable).
    fn canonical_json(value: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<u8> {
        serde_json::to_vec(value).unwrap_or_default()
    }
    
    /// protobuf `Value` -> JSON. Non-finite doubles become null (JSON has no NaN).
    pub fn proto_value_to_json(value: &ProtoValue) -> serde_json::Value {
        use prost_types::value::Kind;
        match &value.kind {
            None | Some(Kind::NullValue(_)) => serde_json::Value::Null,
            Some(Kind::NumberValue(n)) => serde_json::Number::from_f64(*n)
                .map(serde_json::Value::Number)
                .unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null),
            Some(Kind::StringValue(s)) => serde_json::Value::String(s.clone()),
            Some(Kind::BoolValue(b)) => serde_json::Value::Bool(*b),
            Some(Kind::StructValue(s)) => serde_json::Value::Object(
                s.fields
                    .iter()
                    .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), proto_value_to_json(v)))
                    .collect(),
            ),
            Some(Kind::ListValue(l)) => {
                serde_json::Value::Array(l.values.iter().map(proto_value_to_json).collect())
            }
        }
    }
    
    /// JSON -> protobuf `Value`.
    pub fn json_to_proto_value(value: &serde_json::Value) -> ProtoValue {
        use prost_types::value::Kind;
        let kind = match value {
            serde_json::Value::Null => Kind::NullValue(0),
            serde_json::Value::Bool(b) => Kind::BoolValue(*b),
            serde_json::Value::Number(n) => Kind::NumberValue(n.as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0)),
            serde_json::Value::String(s) => Kind::StringValue(s.clone()),
            serde_json::Value::Array(items) => Kind::ListValue(prost_types::ListValue {
                values: items.iter().map(json_to_proto_value).collect(),
            }),
            serde_json::Value::Object(map) => Kind::StructValue(json_map_to_proto_struct(map)),
        };
        ProtoValue { kind: Some(kind) }
    }
    
    /// JSON object -> protobuf `Struct`.
    pub fn json_map_to_proto_struct(
        map: &serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
    ) -> ProtoStruct {
        ProtoStruct {
            fields: map
                .iter()
                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), json_to_proto_value(v)))
                .collect(),
        }
    }
    
    fn deep_merge(
        base: &mut serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
        patch: &serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
    ) {
        for (key, value) in patch {
            match (base.get_mut(key), value) {
                (Some(serde_json::Value::Object(b)), serde_json::Value::Object(p)) => {
                    deep_merge(b, p);
                }
                _ => {
                    base.insert(key.clone(), value.clone());
                }
            }
        }
    }

        async fn call_method(
            &self,
            request: Request<CallMethodRequest>,
        ) -> Result<Response<CallMethodResponse>, Status> {
            let metadata = request.metadata();
            if metadata.get_bin("x-oracle-identity-assertion-bin").is_some() {
                return Err(Status::unauthenticated("oracle admission is not wired"));
            }
            let identity_headers = metadata.get_all_bin(op_identity::sealed_id::HTTP_HEADER_NAME);
            let mut identities = identity_headers.iter();
            let identity = identities
                .next()
                .ok_or_else(|| Status::unauthenticated("missing sealed identity"))?
                .to_bytes()
                .map_err(|_| Status::unauthenticated("invalid sealed identity"))?;
            if identities.next().is_some() {
                return Err(Status::unauthenticated("multiple sealed identities"));

    fn jsonrpc_error(id: serde_json::Value, code: i64, message: &str) -> serde_json::Value {

            "jsonrpc": "2.0",
            "id": id,
            "error": { "code": code, "message": message },
        })

    async fn handle_alias_task(
        State(state): State<AppState>,
        axum::extract::Path(alias): axum::extract::Path<String>,
        headers: HeaderMap,
        body: Result<Json<JsonRpcRequest>, axum::extract::rejection::JsonRejection>,
    ) -> impl IntoResponse {
        if let Err(e) = require_auth(&state, &headers) {
            return e.into_response();
        }
    
        {
            let config = state.config.read();
            if !config.a2a.server.enabled {
                return StatusCode::NOT_FOUND.into_response();
            }
            let published = config
                .agents
                .get(&alias)
                .map(|a| a.enabled && a.a2a.published)
                .unwrap_or(false);
            if !published {
                return StatusCode::NOT_FOUND.into_response();
            }
        }
    
        let Json(req) = match body {
            Ok(req) => req,
            Err(_) => {
                return (
                    StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
                    Json(jsonrpc_error(
                        serde_json::Value::Null,
                        -32700,
                        "Parse error: expected a JSON-RPC 2.0 request",
                    )),
                )
                    .into_response();
            }
        };
    
        if req.jsonrpc != "2.0" {
            return (
                StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
                Json(jsonrpc_error(
                    req.id,
                    -32600,
                    "Invalid request: jsonrpc must be \"2.0\"",
                )),
            )
                .into_response();
        }
    
        if req.method != "message/send" {
            return (
                StatusCode::OK,
                Json(jsonrpc_error(
                    req.id,
                    -32601,
                    "Method not found: only message/send is supported on this build",
                )),
            )
                .into_response();
        }
            Ok(request)
        }

    //! Read committed public state through the pinned plugin policy.
    use std::path::Path;
    
    fn redact_identity_credentials(value: &mut simd_json::OwnedValue) {
        match value {
            simd_json::OwnedValue::Object(object) => {
                object.remove("sealed_id");
                for nested in object.values_mut() {
                    redact_identity_credentials(nested);
                }
            }
            simd_json::OwnedValue::Array(values) => {
                for nested in values {
                    redact_identity_credentials(nested);
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    
    pub(crate) fn public_plugin_value(
        plugin_id: &str,
        value: &simd_json::OwnedValue,
    ) -> simd_json::OwnedValue {
        let mut public = value.clone();
        if plugin_id == "identity_sled" {
            redact_identity_credentials(&mut public);
        }
        public
    }
    
    /// Public state read from the committed projection, not from an event payload.
    pub(crate) struct PublicStateSnapshot {
        pub value: simd_json::OwnedValue,
        pub generation: u64,
        pub schema_hash: String,
    }
    
    /// Read a public projection using one manifest-pinned plugin policy.
    /// Caller authorization is separate and must precede outward disclosure.
    pub(crate) fn read_public_state_in(
        catalog_dir: &Path,
        state_dir: &str,
        plugin_id: &str,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<Option<PublicStateSnapshot>> {
        let before = crate::catalog::Catalog::sealed_plugin(catalog_dir, plugin_id)?;
        let schema: op_state_store::PluginSchema = serde_json::from_value(
            before
                .schema
                .clone()
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("sealed plugin schema unavailable"))?,
        )?;
        let snapshot =
            op_core::projection_shm::read_projection_snapshot_in(state_dir, &[plugin_id.to_owned()])?;
        let after = crate::catalog::Catalog::sealed_plugin(catalog_dir, plugin_id)?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            before.schema_hash == after.schema_hash
                && before.sealed_schema_json == after.sealed_schema_json,
            "sealed plugin changed during state read"
        );
        let Some(mut bytes) = snapshot.states.get(plugin_id).cloned() else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let private = simd_json::to_owned_value(&mut bytes)?;
        let Some(projected) = schema.project_public_state(&private)? else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let public = public_plugin_value(plugin_id, &projected);
        anyhow::ensure!(
            matches!(&public, simd_json::OwnedValue::Object(_)),
            "committed plugin state is not an object"
        );
        Ok(Some(PublicStateSnapshot {
            value: public,
            generation: snapshot.generation,
            schema_hash: before.schema_hash,
        }))
    }

            let catalog_dir = root.path().join("catalog");
            let state_dir = root.path().join("state");
            let state_path = state_dir.to_str().unwrap();
            let schema = op_state_store::PluginSchema::builder("fixture")

                .string_field("secret", false, "")
                .public_state_paths(&["/status"])

            let mut catalog = op_blob::BlobStore::open(&catalog_dir).unwrap();
            let blob = op_blob::blobify_plugin_schema("fixture", schema);

                    .is_none()

    #[async_trait::async_trait]
    impl StateSync for BridgeService {
        type SubscribeStream = ReceiverStream<Result<StateChange, Status>>;
    
        async fn subscribe(
            &self,
            request: Request<SubscribeRequest>,
        ) -> Result<Response<Self::SubscribeStream>, Status> {
            let req = request.into_inner();
            // Register before returning the RPC, and snapshot under the same
            // commit boundary. No updates can fall between hydration and live.
            let (initial, schemas, mut sub) = self.core.state_subscription(
                req.include_initial_state,
                req.include_schema,
            );
            let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel(128);
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                for frame in initial {
                    if state_matches(&req, &frame) && tx.send(Ok(frame)).await.is_err() {
                        return;
                    }
                }
                for frame in schemas {
                    // Contracts carry no path or tags; the plugin filter still applies.
                    if !req.plugin_ids.is_empty() && !req.plugin_ids.contains(&frame.plugin_id) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    if tx.send(Ok(frame)).await.is_err() {
                        return;
                    }
                }
                loop {
                    let received = tokio::select! {
                        _ = tx.closed() => return,
                        received = sub.recv() => received,
                    };
                    match received {
                        Ok(frame) => {
                            if state_matches(&req, &frame) && tx.send(Ok(frame)).await.is_err() {
                                return;
                            }
                        }
                        Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(skipped)) => {
                            let _ = tx.send(Err(Status::data_loss(format!(
                                "state stream missed {skipped} updates; resubscribe with include_initial_state",
                            )))).await;
                            return;
                        }
                        Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => return,
                    }
                }
            });
            Ok(Response::new(ReceiverStream::new(rx)))

        /// Production always uses [`Self::from_env`], which defaults to
        /// `trusted-decoy-signature`.
        pub fn new(trust_store: DecoyTrustStore) -> Self {
            Self {
                trust_store,
                replay_cache: AssertionReplayCache::new(CLOCK_LEEWAY_SECS),
                leeway_secs: CLOCK_LEEWAY_SECS,
                max_lifetime_secs: MAX_LIFETIME_SECS as i64,

        /// Construct the production validator, reading the transport-binding
        /// selector. Missing or unknown `OP_ORACLE_ASSERTION_SOURCE_BINDING` uses
        /// `trusted-decoy-signature` (the live fabric binding). `exact-peer-ip`
        /// remains available as an explicit legacy opt-in.
        pub fn from_env(trust_store: DecoyTrustStore) -> Self {
            let path = std::env::var(AUTH_REPLAY_DB_PATH_ENV)
                .map(PathBuf::from)
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from(DEFAULT_AUTH_REPLAY_DB_PATH));
            let replay_cache = match AssertionReplayCache::persistent(&path, CLOCK_LEEWAY_SECS) {
                Ok(cache) => cache,
                Err(error) => {
                    tracing::error!(path = %path.display(), %error, "durable auth replay store unavailable");
                    AssertionReplayCache::unavailable(error.to_string(), CLOCK_LEEWAY_SECS)
                }
            };
            let mut validator = Self::new(trust_store)
                .with_replay_cache(replay_cache)
                .with_source_binding(AssertionSourceBinding::from_env());
            validator.browser_binding = BrowserBindingPolicy::from_env();
            validator
        }
    
        pub fn with_source_binding(mut self, source_binding: AssertionSourceBinding) -> Self {
            self.source_binding = source_binding;
            self

    impl SchemaBackedInterface {
        /// Generic method call dispatcher.
        ///
        /// All schema-defined methods are funneled through this call, allowing
        /// dynamic dispatch without compile-time traits for every plugin.
        ///
        /// Dispatch pipeline (Requirement 7):
        ///   1. Method lookup → reject if not declared (UnknownMethod)
        ///   2. Arg validation → reject if invalid (InvalidArgs)
        ///   3. Capability check → reject if required_capability not granted (AccessDenied)
        ///   4. MutationEngine.mutate → record in event chain (Requirement 5)
        async fn call(
            &self,
            method: String,
            json_args: String,
            #[zbus(header)] header: Header<'_>,
        ) -> zbus::fdo::Result<String> {
            if let Some(receiver) = &self.mcp_identity {
                let identity = receiver
                    .resolve()
                    .await
                    .map_err(|error| zbus::fdo::Error::AccessDenied(error.to_string()))?;
                return self
                    .dispatch_call_for_identity(method, json_args, Some(&identity))
                    .await;
            }
            if let Some(lungs) = &self.lungs_identity {
                let identity = lungs
                    .resolve()
                    .await
                    .map_err(|error| zbus::fdo::Error::AccessDenied(error.to_string()))?;
                return self
                    .dispatch_call_for_identity(method, json_args, Some(&identity))
                    .await;
            }
            let resolver = self.identity_resolver.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {
                zbus::fdo::Error::AccessDenied("D-Bus identity resolver is not available".to_string())
            })?;
            let identity = resolver
                .resolve(&header)
                .await
                .map_err(|error| zbus::fdo::Error::AccessDenied(error.to_string()))?;
            self.dispatch_call_for_identity(method, json_args, Some(&identity))
                .await
        }
    
        /// Same admission as Call, with caller-scoped correlation retained before
        /// submission. This identifier is never identity or capability evidence.
        async fn call_with_operation_id(
            &self,
            method: String,
            json_args: String,
            operation_id: String,
            #[zbus(header)] header: Header<'_>,
        ) -> zbus::fdo::Result<String> {
            let parsed = uuid::Uuid::parse_str(&operation_id)
                .map_err(|_| zbus::fdo::Error::InvalidArgs("invalid operation id".into()))?;
            if parsed.to_string() != operation_id {
                return Err(zbus::fdo::Error::InvalidArgs(
                    "noncanonical operation id".into(),
                ));
            }

    #!/bin/sh
    # Keep the control-plane chatbot's existing identity container running.
    # Starts and stops the Incus instance only; storage, Btrfs members and the
    # identity record stay with their owners. Humans start at login in the bridge.
    exec 2>&1
    NAME=${CHATBOT_CONTAINER:-3tchedCtlChatbot}
    rm -f /run/opdbus/runit-ready/chatbot-identity
    sv start incus >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    i=0
    until incus info >/dev/null 2>&1; do
        i=$((i + 1))
        [ "$i" -lt 90 ] || { echo 'incusd API not ready after 90s' >&2; exit 1; }
        sleep 1
    done
    state() { incus list -f csv -c s "^${NAME}\$" 2>/dev/null; }
    [ -n "$(state)" ] || { echo "container $NAME does not exist" >&2; exit 1; }
    if [ "$(state)" != RUNNING ]; then
        echo "starting $NAME"
        incus start "$NAME" || { incus info "$NAME" --show-log 2>&1 | tail -n 40; exit 1; }
    fi
    i=0
    until [ "$(state)" = RUNNING ]; do
        i=$((i + 1))
        [ "$i" -lt 60 ] || { echo "$NAME did not reach RUNNING" >&2; exit 1; }
        sleep 1
    done
    echo "$NAME is RUNNING"
    install -d -m 755 /run/opdbus/runit-ready
    : > /run/opdbus/runit-ready/chatbot-identity
    trap 'echo "stopping $NAME"; incus stop "$NAME" --timeout 30 || incus stop "$NAME" --force; exit 0' TERM INT HUP
    while [ "$(state)" = RUNNING ]; do sleep 5 & wait $!; done
    echo "$NAME left RUNNING; exiting for restart"
    exit 1
    //! Shared identity-to-container and human binding checks.
    use op_plugins::state_plugins::identity_sled::ContainerIdentitySled;
    use op_plugins::state_plugins::incus::IncusInstance;
    
    pub(crate) const CONTROL_PLANE_CHATBOT_CONTAINER: &str = "3tchedChatbot";
    pub(crate) const RESERVED_CHATBOT_CONTAINER: &str = "3tchedCtlChatbot";
    
    pub fn configured_chatbot_key() -> Option<String> {
        std::env::var("OP_CONTROL_PLANE_CHATBOT_WIREGUARD_PUBKEY")
            .ok()
            .map(|value| value.trim().to_owned())
            .filter(|value| !value.is_empty())
    }
    
    fn chatbot_binding_matches(
        sled: &ContainerIdentitySled,
        instance: &IncusInstance,
        configured_session: Option<&str>,
        configured_key: Option<&str>,
    ) -> bool {
        instance.name == CONTROL_PLANE_CHATBOT_CONTAINER
            && instance.instance_type == "container"
            && sled.principal_kind.as_deref() == Some("service")
            && configured_session == Some(sled.session_id.as_str())
            && configured_key == Some(sled.wireguard_pubkey.as_str())
            && op_identity::session::derive_session_id(&sled.wireguard_pubkey) == sled.session_id
            && instance.config.as_ref().is_some_and(|config| {
                config.get("user.opdbus.session_id") == Some(&sled.session_id)
                    && config.get("user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key") == Some(&sled.wireguard_pubkey)
            })
    }
    
    pub fn identity_instance_matches(sled: &ContainerIdentitySled, instance: &IncusInstance) -> bool {
        // The native name is a label. Ownership remains the stored UUID, session
        // and key binding, not the label's number or its creation receipt.
        let named = (op_cozo_store::is_numbered_native_name(&instance.name)
            || (instance.name == RESERVED_CHATBOT_CONTAINER
                && sled.principal_kind.as_deref() == Some("service")
                && control_plane_chatbot_session_id().as_deref() == Some(sled.session_id.as_str())
                && configured_chatbot_key().as_deref() == Some(sled.wireguard_pubkey.as_str())
                && op_identity::session::derive_session_id(&sled.wireguard_pubkey) == sled.session_id))
            && instance.instance_type == "container"
            && instance.config.as_ref().is_some_and(|c| {
                c.get("user.opdbus.session_id") == Some(&sled.session_id)
                    && c.get("user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key") == Some(&sled.wireguard_pubkey)
                    && c.get("volatile.uuid")
                        .is_some_and(|v| uuid::Uuid::parse_str(v).is_ok())
            })
            && sled.instance.as_ref().is_some_and(|stored| {
                stored.name == instance.name
                    && stored
                        .config
                        .as_ref()
                        .zip(instance.config.as_ref())
                        .is_some_and(|(a, b)| a.get("volatile.uuid") == b.get("volatile.uuid"))
            });
        named
            || (instance.name == sled.session_id && instance.instance_type == "container")
            || chatbot_binding_matches(
                sled,
                instance,
                control_plane_chatbot_session_id().as_deref(),
                configured_chatbot_key().as_deref(),
            )
    }
    
    pub fn identity_session_binding_matches(sled: &ContainerIdentitySled) -> bool {
        match sled.instance.as_ref() {
            Some(instance) => identity_instance_matches(sled, instance),
            // The identity owner explicitly initializes humans without per-account
            // containers. Actor class comes from the committed record, not SID1 or
            // request metadata; any attached instance must still match above.
            None => sled.principal_kind.as_deref() == Some("human"),
        }
    }
    
    pub fn validate_sled(sled: &ContainerIdentitySled) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        anyhow::ensure!(!sled.session_id.is_empty(), "identity session id is empty");
        anyhow::ensure!(
            sled.mutation_index <= i64::MAX as u64,
            "mutation index overflow"
        );
        if let Some(instance) = &sled.instance {
            anyhow::ensure!(
                identity_instance_matches(sled, instance),
                "identity instance does not match session container"
            );
        }
        if sled.is_anchored() {
            anyhow::ensure!(
                sled.sealed_id
                    .as_deref()
                    .is_some_and(|value| !value.is_empty()),
                "anchored identity lacks authored SID1"
            );
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    /// Session id of the control-plane chatbot, from
    /// `OP_CONTROL_PLANE_CHATBOT_SESSION_ID`.
    pub fn control_plane_chatbot_session_id() -> Option<String> {
        std::env::var("OP_CONTROL_PLANE_CHATBOT_SESSION_ID")
            .ok()
            .map(|value| value.trim().to_string())
            .filter(|value| !value.is_empty())
    }

            let mut sled: ContainerIdentitySled = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::json!({

            assert!(identity_session_binding_matches(&sled));

            sled.instance = Some(

                }))
                .unwrap(),
            );
            assert!(identity_session_binding_matches(&sled));
            sled.instance.as_mut().unwrap().name = "other".into();
            assert!(!identity_session_binding_matches(&sled));
        }

    # Provision a dedicated native profile through the binary's config owner.

    set -eu

    # Providers whose model lists the model_registry plugin keeps current.
    #
    # Installed root-owned at /etc/op-dbus/model-providers.toml. The list is the
    # owner's keyed inference providers: each names the variable in the owner's
    # ~/.bash_secrets its key comes from (key_env), and
    # `sudo scripts/install-provider-keys.sh` copies those keys into the
    # root-owned key files below. A provider whose key file is missing shows as a
    # failed refresh and offers no models.
    #
    # The control-plane chatbot calls model_registry.refresh hourly through its
    # lungs: each enabled provider is asked for its current models, new ones are
    # added, and models a provider stops listing stay in the catalog marked
    # unavailable. OpenCode and OpenRouter change their lists often, which is why
    # this is refreshed rather than written down.
    #
    # Fields: id (lowercase, digits, _), name, models_url (https), format
    # ("openai" or "anthropic" response shape), auth ("none", "bearer" or
    # "x_api_key"), key_file (root-owned 0400/0600 file directly under
    # /etc/op-dbus/secrets/, required unless auth = "none"), key_env (the
    # ~/.bash_secrets variable it is installed from), enabled (default true),
    # native_provider_id (the exact ordinary-selection family.alias, separate
    # from id), inference_url_prefix (the platform API namespace the route
    # checks require), and control_plane: the tched-router profile (family.alias)
    # that serves this provider's models for the Control Plane, plus any
    # alternative profiles the provider offers (another wire format on the same
    # provider). A key is only ever sent to its own provider.
    #
    # Credential gate (moved out of the retired ~/.bash_models flag file; TOML
    # syntax, one file). Each entry may declare `credential = "key" | "oauth" |
    # "off"` and, for oauth only, `credential_slot`. Slots are references, never
    # credential values: a keyed entry's slot is its key_env (or its key_file
    # when the key is installed directly, like opencode_go); an oauth entry's
    # slot is the native auth profile id (`family:profile`); an `off` entry
    # retains its key_env for the later re-enable. When `credential` is absent
    # the plain `enabled` flag governs (migration-safe). An `off` entry is hidden
    # and never refreshed; an `oauth` entry runs no keyed discovery (its rows
    # come from the native profile inventory, not the API key). Unknown class
    # text or a broken slot pairing fails the whole parse. The LLM maintains
    # these columns through model_registry.maintain_credentials.
    #
    # This file lists providers only. Models change constantly and are never
    # written here: the catalog holds them, and the control-plane LLM records per
    # model which of its provider's profiles it needs (model_registry
    # set_model_profile).
    
    # OpenCode Go. Its key is not in ~/.bash_secrets; it is installed directly as
    # /etc/op-dbus/secrets/opencode-api-key (the router already requires it).
    # Slot = key_file.
    [[providers]]
    id = "opencode_go"
    native_provider_id = "opencode.go_dashboard"
    inference_url_prefix = "https://opencode.ai/zen/go"
    name = "OpenCode Go"
    models_url = "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/models"
    format = "openai"
    auth = "bearer"
    key_file = "/etc/op-dbus/secrets/opencode-api-key"
    credential = "key"
    control_plane = { profile = "opencode.go_control_plane", alternatives = [
      "anthropic.go_control_plane_messages",
      "opencode.go_control_plane_responses",
    ] }
    
    [[providers]]

    format = "openai"

    # Initialize the requested control-plane route once, through ZeroClaw's config owner.
    set -eu
    [ "$#" -eq 0 ] || exit 2
    config=/var/lib/zeroclaw
    binary=/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/threetched/threetched
    key=/etc/op-dbus/secrets/meta-model-api-key
    [ -f "$key" ] && [ ! -L "$key" ] || exit 0
    case "$(stat -c %u:%a "$key")" in 0:400|0:600) ;; *) exit 78 ;; esac
    native_config() {
        chpst -u root:root env HOME="$config/home" USER=root \
            "$binary" config "$@" --config-dir "$config"
    }
    existing=$(native_config get providers.models.custom.muse_code_control_plane.model --json 2>/dev/null || true)

    ---
    name: systematic-debugging
    description: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
    ---
    
    # Systematic Debugging
    
    ## Overview
    
    **Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.
    
    **Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**
    
    ## The Iron Law
    
    ```
    NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
    ```
    
    If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.
    
    ## When to Use
    
    Use for ANY technical issue:
    - Test failures
    - Bugs in production
    - Unexpected behavior
    - Performance problems
    - Build failures
    - Integration issues
    
    **Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
    - Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
    - "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
    - You've already tried multiple fixes
    - Previous fix didn't work
    - You don't fully understand the issue
    
    **Don't skip when:**
    - Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
    - You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
    - Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)
    
    ## The Four Phases
    
    You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
    
    ### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation
    
    **BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**
    
    1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
       - Don't skip past errors or warnings
       - They often contain the exact solution
       - Read stack traces completely
       - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes
    
    2. **Reproduce Consistently**
       - Can you trigger it reliably?
       - What are the exact steps?
       - Does it happen every time?
       - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess
    
    3. **Check Recent Changes**
       - What changed that could cause this?
       - Git diff, recent commits
       - New dependencies, config changes
       - Environmental differences
    
    4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**
    
       **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**
    
       **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
       ```
       For EACH component boundary:
         - Log what data enters component
         - Log what data exits component
         - Verify environment/config propagation
         - Check state at each layer
    
       Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
       THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
       THEN investigate that specific component
       ```
    
       **Example (multi-layer system):**
       ```bash
       # Layer 1: Workflow
       echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
       echo "IDENTITY: $([ -n "${IDENTITY:-}" ] && echo SET || echo UNSET)"
    
       # Layer 2: Build script
       echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
       printenv IDENTITY >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "IDENTITY in environment" || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"
    
       # Layer 3: Signing script
       echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
       security list-keychains
       security find-identity -v
    
       # Layer 4: Actual signing
       codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
       ```
    
       **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)
    
    5. **Trace Data Flow**
    
       **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**
    
       See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.
    
       **Quick version:**
       - Where does bad value originate?
       - What called this with bad value?
       - Keep tracing up until you find the source
       - Fix at source, not at symptom
    
    ### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis
    
    **Find the pattern before fixing:**
    
    1. **Find Working Examples**
       - Locate similar working code in same codebase
       - What works that's similar to what's broken?
    
    2. **Compare Against References**
       - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
       - Don't skim - read every line
       - Understand the pattern fully before applying
    
    3. **Identify Differences**
       - What's different between working and broken?
       - List every difference, however small
       - Don't assume "that can't matter"
    
    4. **Understand Dependencies**
       - What other components does this need?
       - What settings, config, environment?
       - What assumptions does it make?
    
    ### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing
    
    **Scientific method:**
    
    1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
       - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
       - Write it down
       - Be specific, not vague
    
    2. **Test Minimally**
       - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
       - One variable at a time
       - Don't fix multiple things at once
    
    3. **Verify Before Continuing**
       - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
       - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
       - DON'T add more fixes on top
    
    4. **When You Don't Know**
       - Say "I don't understand X"
       - Don't pretend to know
       - Ask for help
       - Research more
    
    ### Phase 4: Implementation
    
    **Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**
    
    1. **Create Failing Test Case**
       - Simplest possible reproduction
       - Automated test if possible
       - One-off test script if no framework
       - MUST have before fixing
       - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests
    
    2. **Implement Single Fix**
       - Address the root cause identified
       - ONE change at a time
       - No "while I'm here" improvements
       - No bundled refactoring
    
    3. **Verify Fix**
       - Test passes now?
       - No other tests broken?
       - Issue actually resolved?
       - Use the `superpowers:verification-before-completion` skill before claiming success
    
    4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
       - STOP
       - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
       - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
       - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
       - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion
    
    5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**
    
       **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
       - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
       - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
       - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere
    
       **STOP and question fundamentals:**
       - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
       - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
       - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?
    
       **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**
    
       This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.
    
    ## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process
    
    If you catch yourself thinking:
    - "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
    - "Just try changing X and see if it works"
    - "Add multiple changes, run tests"
    - "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
    - "It's probably X, let me fix that"
    - "I don't fully understand but this might work"
    - "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
    - "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
    - Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
    - **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
    - **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**
    
    **ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**
    
    **If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)
    
    ## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong
    
    **Watch for these redirections:**
    - "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
    - "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
    - "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
    - "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
    - "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working
    
    **When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.
    
    ## Common Rationalizations
    
    | Excuse | Reality |
    |--------|---------|
    | "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
    | "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
    | "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
    | "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
    | "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
    | "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
    | "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
    | "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |
    
    ## Quick Reference
    
    | Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
    |-------|---------------|------------------|
    | **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
    | **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
    | **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
    | **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |
    
    ## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"
    
    If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:
    
    1. You've completed the process
    2. Document what you investigated
    3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
    4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation
    
    **But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.
    
    ## Supporting Techniques
    
    These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:
    
    - **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
    - **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
    - **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

    //! gRPC Client - For D-Bus → remote gRPC calls
    //!
    //! Allows local D-Bus services to call remote gRPC endpoints,
    //! enabling distributed operation-dbus deployments.
    
    use std::collections::HashMap;
    use std::sync::Arc;
    use std::time::Duration;
    
    use base64::Engine as _;
    use prost_types::{Struct as ProstStruct, Value as ProstValue, value::Kind as ProstKind};
    use tokio::sync::RwLock;
    use tonic::Request;
    use tonic::metadata::MetadataValue;
    use tonic::transport::{Certificate, Channel, ClientTlsConfig, Endpoint};
    use tracing::info;
    
    use crate::proto::{
        CallMethodRequest, GetStateRequest, GetStateResponse, MutateRequest,
        OperationType as ProtoOperationType, SubscribeEventsRequest, SubscribeRequest,
        event_chain_service_client::EventChainServiceClient,
        plugin_service_client::PluginServiceClient, state_sync_client::StateSyncClient,
    };
    
    /// Bounded response envelope for complete plugin documents and SHM state.
    /// Native chat can exceed tonic's 4 MiB default; identity admission is unchanged.
    pub const MAX_PLUGIN_STATE_RESPONSE_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
    
    
    /// Configuration for a remote gRPC endpoint
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub struct RemoteEndpoint {
        pub address: String,
        pub tls_enabled: bool,
        pub connect_timeout: Duration,
        pub request_timeout: Duration,
    }
    
    /// Caller-supplied Ghostbridge identity forwarded by an HTTP compatibility
    /// adapter into the canonical gRPC method call.
    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub struct GhostbridgeCallMetadata {
        /// Exact caller-supplied SID1 wire bytes, if this is a local identity call.
        pub sealed_id: Option<Vec<u8>>,
        /// Exact caller-supplied OIA1 wire bytes, if this is a decoy assertion call.
        pub oracle_assertion: Option<Vec<u8>>,
        /// Legacy fields retained for non-plugin Ghostbridge services.
        pub session_genesis: Option<String>,
        pub trace_id: Option<String>,
        pub wireguard_pubkey: Option<String>,
    }
    
    impl Default for RemoteEndpoint {
        fn default() -> Self {
            Self {
                address: "http://127.0.0.1:8090".to_string(),
                tls_enabled: false,
                connect_timeout: Duration::from_secs(5),
                request_timeout: Duration::from_secs(30),
            }
        }
    }
    
    /// gRPC client pool for connecting to remote Operation services
    pub struct GrpcClientPool {
        /// Map of endpoint address to channel
        channels: RwLock<HashMap<String, Channel>>,
        /// Default endpoint configuration
        default_config: RemoteEndpoint,
    }
    
    impl Default for GrpcClientPool {
        fn default() -> Self {
            Self::new()
        }
    }
    
    impl GrpcClientPool {
        pub fn new() -> Self {
            Self {
                channels: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
                default_config: RemoteEndpoint::default(),
            }
        }
    
        pub fn with_default_config(config: RemoteEndpoint) -> Self {
            Self {
                channels: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
                default_config: config,
            }
        }
    
        /// Apply transport settings (timeouts + TLS) to an endpoint.
        ///
        /// TLS is driven by the URI scheme: `https://` gets a tonic
        /// `ClientTlsConfig`. This mirrors `examples/repro_subscribe.rs`, which is
        /// the reference client path. Trust anchors, in priority order:
        ///   1. `OP_DBUS_GRPC_CA_FILE` — PEM file to pin (what op-web's run script
        ///      exports; may point at the leaf cert itself since it is its own CA).
        ///   2. Native system roots (`with_native_roots`).
        ///
        /// `OP_DBUS_GRPC_TLS_DOMAIN` overrides the SNI/verification name when the
        /// dial address is an IP or differs from the certificate SAN.

    //! ChatService gRPC server implementation.
    //!
    //! Implements the `op_chat.chat.ChatService` trait from `chat.proto`.
    //!
    //! Architecture:
    //! - threetched owns provider/model routing (OD-28) — SendRequest carries them.
    //! - gemma_brain routes to the selected model and applies compliance tags.
    //! - The chatbot is a DELEGATOR — forced tool calling is mandatory; even user
    //!   responses are emitted as tool calls (respond_to_user).
    //! - Chat persistence flows through the memory loop → cognitive.
    //! - The agent loop is bounded (≥50 steps) and cancellable.

    fn stage_shm() -> Result<(), String> {

                persisted.display()
